--- MCD-1425 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Duel That Would Cost Nothing But Him" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-duel-that-would-cost-nothing-but-him.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XCV, wave 32. First entry to stage an entire engagement with the Trinity excluded from the terms before it begins rather than merely unused or malfunctioning: a garrison commander offers formal single combat, plain blade only, to decide an entire siege's outcome and spare both sides further casualties. Bane accepts on those exact terms -- Onyx sheathed, Mafesto and Obsidian Malice left with the column -- and wins through patience and Valen Sinisterblade's own training (MCD-291/292) rather than any augmented power, isolating his raw swordsmanship as the sole deciding factor for the first time since 'The Fight He Couldn't Walk Away From' (MCD-476), which still involved Onyx. The garrison surrenders whole per the wager's terms. No new named characters -- the commander is unnamed and one-scene; Corren Halst reused.

--- MCD-939 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Council That Asked Him to Speak Plainly" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-council-that-asked-him-to-speak-plainly.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LV, wave 19. A neutral cross-faction arbiter council summons Bane to answer fabricated and exaggerated atrocity claims; he testifies disarmed, answering honestly for real failures while refusing accusations the record doesn't support. First formal institutional/legal-tribunal register for this alias.

--- MCD-706 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Promise He Couldn't Keep" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-promise-he-couldnt-keep.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XLI, wave 14 of ten (waves 6-15). A specific date-certain promise to defend a settlement is broken due to an unavoidable crisis elsewhere, costing four lives; Bane owns it fully and permanently changes how he frames future assurances -- the presence trait's failure from his own side.

--- MCD-1426 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"What the Enemy's Own Children Were Owed" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/what-the-enemys-own-children-were-owed.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XCVI, wave 32, closing wave 32. First entry to extend 'the fear only works if it's true' (MCD-431) to the dependents of enemy soldiers rather than to enemies, civilians, or captives themselves: the same supply-chain sabotage that starved the Threshbend depot into surrender (MCD-700) is found to be reaching a garrison town's own military families, and Bane redirects captured grain to the civilian quarter over Corren Halst's strategic objection, stating the campaign's target was the garrison's capacity to fight, not its children's next meal. No new named characters -- the woman and her family are unnamed; Corren Halst and Danne Sok reused. Closes wave 32.

--- MCD-700 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Grain That Never Reached the Garrison" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-grain-that-never-reached-the-garrison.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XXXV, wave 12 of ten (waves 6-15). An eleven-week bloodless siege-by-starvation via deniable, patient supply-chain sabotage forces a 400-man garrison to surrender without a single casualty on either side.

--- MCD-529 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Siege That Took Nine Days" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-siege-that-took-nine-days.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XIV. A detailed, sustained multi-day combat showcase against the fortified Threshbend depot: eight days of invisible psychological pressure (disappearing guard posts, no visible attack) break the garrison's morale before a decisive ninth-day strike -- the first sustained siege-length engagement in the Bane Chronicle series, extending the alias's patience-over-speed principle. No new named characters.

--- MCD-693 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"What He Didn't Say Out Loud" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/what-he-didnt-say-out-loud.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XXVIII, wave 10 of ten (waves 6-15). A private, unguarded late-night conversation with Garren Hask reveals Bane's real, undiminished emotional weight over every death, and his fear of ever becoming numb to it -- the first direct interior/psychological entry.

--- MCD-687 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Pass That Wanted Him Dead First" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-pass-that-wanted-him-dead-first.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XXII, wave 8 of ten (waves 6-15). A pure survival showcase -- Bane and four others cross a lethal mountain pass in a storm to resupply a besieged post, no enemy involved, establishing his ordinary human vulnerability to cold and altitude.

--- MCD-477 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"What the Delay Cost" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/what-the-delay-cost.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XI. Bane's cautious extra-day verification before a prisoner liberation -- the same caution that keeps his reputation honest -- costs two prisoners their lives to an informant embedded among the guards rather than the captives, a genuine failure Bane does not excuse or resolve, the first entry to dramatize a real cost of his own decision-making rather than an external limit. No new named characters.

--- MCD-1061 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Weight Maret Vos Chose to Carry" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-weight-maret-vos-chose-to-carry.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LXIII, closing wave 21. Rebellion era, within the "Bane" window -- not a territory Chronicle. Direct payoff to wave 18's "What He Couldn't Be in Two Places For" (MCD-938), which established Bane splitting the column and trusting Maret Vos (already locked, he/him per the Batch 226 pronoun reconciliation) to run an interception alone. Three weeks later, Maret Vos privately admits he spent the operation's first hour waiting for Bane to arrive and take the plan back, and had deliberately set the ambush closer to the road than necessary to leave room for that. Bane confirms he saw the same tell in the plan's own positioning and chose not to say anything beforehand, stating the distinction plainly: Maret Vos didn't need his plan fixed, he needed to find out for himself that he didn't need Bane to fix it, and only the second was Bane's to give. Gives Maret Vos his own dedicated reflective perspective within Bane's own run for the first time, distinct from his already-locked earlier-crew trilogy entries under the Trench Monarch ("What Maret Vos Carried From Before") and Captain ("The Night Maret Vos Almost Walked") aliases, neither of which this entry repeats or restages. No new named characters -- Maret Vos, Bane, Corren Halst, and Danne Sok reused. Closes wave 21.

--- MCD-365 | category: kanja-chronicle
"The Pivotal Piece" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-pivotal-piece.md), a standalone Kanja-era scene, not a territory Chronicle. Rebellion era, age 19, the night after the Battle of the Black Trench (MCD-232), under the "Bane" alias -- the Directorate's own classification for a threat that destroys the force built to destroy it (MCD-232). An unnamed senior Sovereign Trust Undersecretary comes to the sealed ravine under parley, offering Bane a House seat, a new name, and protection in exchange for standing down, on behalf of "the people who actually hold the ledgers this world runs on." Bane, without standing or raising his voice, delivers the line "I am the pivotal piece to the scheme of all things. Not the Trust's scheme. Not yours... You can't buy a piece that was never on your board" -- a declaration that he answers to something outside the Trust's frame entirely, not a boast or a threat the Undersecretary can report as one. The scene is the first on-page dramatization of the "Already-Finished Negotiation" standing presence trait (VB-060). The closing paragraph plants a deliberate, unscripted forward link to the line's later fame under the Scourge/pirate-era persona (ages 48-52) -- legend's own drift across aliases, not a scripted callback. No new named characters; the Undersecretary is unnamed and one-scene.

--- MCD-1393 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Nights Toran Commanded Alone" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-nights-toran-commanded-alone.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XCIII, wave 31, closing wave 31. Direct payoff to 'The Lieutenant Corren Halst Chose' (MCD-1099) and 'The Weight Maret Vos Chose to Carry' (MCD-1061): Toran requests and runs a full extraction operation with neither Corren Halst nor Bane present at all, the first fully unsupervised test of the crew's trained discipline. His own second-set-of-eyes verification practice (extending MCD-1059's standing order) holds independently, and he talks himself out of sending for confirmation, an explicit, unforced parallel to VB-060's 'Already-Finished Negotiation' presence trait, framing it as a teachable discipline rather than a quality unique to Bane. No new named characters -- Toran (MCD-1099) and Corren Halst reused. Closes wave 31.

--- MCD-1027 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Officer Who Wasn't Lying" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-officer-who-wasnt-lying.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LIX, wave 20. Extends VB-060's "Already-Finished Negotiation" presence trait in reverse: an unnamed Directorate captain approaches Bane alone and unarmed to genuinely defect, and Bane -- who has spent years reading rooms for hidden deception -- finds none, which unsettles him more than any trap would have. Verified over six weeks through Danne Sok's network before being taken in, but believed from the first sentence. First entry to test the presence trait against sincerity rather than performance. No new named characters -- Danne Sok and Callum Breck referenced consistently with their already-locked roles; the defecting captain deliberately left unnamed. Second entry in wave 20.

--- MCD-1100 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"What the River Carried Between Them" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/what-the-river-carried-between-them.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LXX, wave 24. A detailed full-Trinity combat showcase fought waist-deep during a night river crossing under attack: Mafesto redirects the current itself against wading attackers, Onyx's Cadence Ruin reads coordinated footsteps through the riverbed in place of sight, and Obsidian Malice's discharge is deliberately released clear of the water rather than through it to avoid endangering the forty people still crossing -- a new explicit safety constraint on the weapon. No new named characters -- Danne Sok reused. Opens wave 24.

--- MCD-1113 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Weight of the Ones Who Didn't Run" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-weight-of-the-ones-who-didnt-run.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LXXXIII, wave 28. A detailed full-Trinity combat showcase defending a dense urban tenement district whose residents refused evacuation, civilians embedded throughout the fighting rather than cleared ahead of it -- Mafesto's redirections are aimed along streets rather than into structures, Onyx's Cadence Ruin and reading of occupied doorways make the precision possible, and Obsidian Malice is withheld entirely as unsuitable for the terrain, decided before the engagement rather than constrained mid-use. No new named characters -- Efa Gol reused.

--- MCD-1432 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Story That Outran Him" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-story-that-outran-him.md), Bane Alias Chronicle CII, wave 34, closing wave 34 and the thirty-second through thirty-fourth wave run. A trader mentions, in passing, an unverified small uprising three provinces away invoking Bane's name, in a region he has never visited and has no way to reach, confirm, or correct -- extends the legend-drift theme of 'The Song They Sang Without Knowing Whose It Was' (MCD-1108) and 'The Impersonator's Price' (MCD-1428) into its furthest, least controllable form, deliberately left permanently unresolved. No new named characters -- the trader is unnamed and one-scene; Efa Gol and Corren Halst reused. Closes wave 34.

--- MCD-1108 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Song They Sang Without Knowing Whose It Was" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-song-they-sang-without-knowing-whose-it-was.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LXXVIII, wave 26, closing wave 26. Refugee children turn garbled accounts of Bane into a marching song, unaware the man walking near the column's rear is its subject; Bane deliberately doesn't correct it, telling Danne Sok the song isn't about him anymore, it's about what the column needed to believe on a long walk. New folk-culture/legend-drift texture -- uncommercial, uninstitutional, specifically generational -- distinct from prior legend-drift entries. No new named characters -- Danne Sok reused.

--- MCD-1429 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Wedding at the Waystation" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-wedding-at-the-waystation.md), Bane Alias Chronicle XCIX, wave 33, closing wave 33. Bane's first purely celebratory, entirely conflict-free entry: Toran (already locked, MCD-1099) marries a woman from a settlement freed three months earlier, and the column halts a full evening for the ceremony, with Bane standing as witness at Toran's request. No tactical, combat, or gear dimension of any kind -- distinct from every prior warm/personal register in the run, all of which still carried the war's weight directly in the scene. No new named characters -- the bride is deliberately left unnamed; Toran, Efa Gol, Danne Sok, and Corren Halst reused. Closes wave 33.

--- MCD-432 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Full Weight of the Trinity" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-full-weight-of-the-trinity.md), Bane Alias Chronicle VIII. A detailed single-combat Trinity showcase against the fortified Kessic Overwatch garrison: Mafesto's Kinetic Transfer System absorbing a six-impact volley into stored charge, Obsidian Malice's two-year dormant charge breaching the inner gate in one strike, and Onyx of Oblivion's Cadence Ruin/Veil Piercer breaking a trained formation into six isolated fighters, ending with the garrison's surrender and the Trinity's remaining charge deliberately left unspent. No new named characters.

--- MCD-1060 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Twelve Miles That Never Stopped Moving" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-twelve-miles-that-never-stopped-moving.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LXII, wave 21. Rebellion era, within the "Bane" window -- not a territory Chronicle. A detailed full-Trinity combat showcase built around continuous motion rather than a held position: a six-hundred-refugee convoy, a wounded rearguard, and a pursuing Directorate cavalry screen force a twelve-mile defense across three changing terrains without the column's pace ever dropping below a walk, since stopping to fight properly would win the battle but cost the two remaining daylight hours needed to reach the border crossing. Across open grassland, Mafesto's Kinetic Transfer System redirects charging cavalry's own momentum sideways through Bane's footing mid-stride, dropping horse and rider without a halt in the column's march. Through a close pine stand, Onyx of Oblivion's Cadence Ruin folds an infantry bottleneck attempt apart before it reaches striking range while Veil Piercer picks two disguised scouts out of a civilian-looking knot mid-stride. Along a final exposed causeway, Obsidian Malice's two-year dormant charge is released in one arcing discharge timed to the pursuing commander's committed final push, delivered without Bane breaking stride to aim it. The column crosses the border zone an hour before dusk having never once formed up to fight from fixed ground. Distinguished from every prior full-Trinity showcase (the fortified-garrison assault, MCD-432; the multi-day siege, MCD-529; the vertical battlement fight, MCD-703; the precision-constrained bridge defense, MCD-1026; and the most-intense ravine battle, MCD-709) by its continuous-motion constraint, requiring all three Trinity pieces to operate at pace across shifting terrain in one unbroken line of march rather than from a held position. No new named characters -- Efa Gol reused; the pursuing Directorate commander is unnamed and one-scene. Second entry in wave 21.

--- MCD-1097 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Charge That Fired Too Soon" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-charge-that-fired-too-soon.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LXVII, wave 23. First genuine Obsidian Malice equipment failure for this alias: an electrical storm's ambient charge triggers a partial premature discharge mid-approach to a garrison, costing surprise; Bane adapts and wins anyway through improvisation, and openly acknowledges the failure to the crew afterward. Extends the weapon's established two-timescale charge mechanism with a new environmental-interference case, completing a documented failure case for all three Trinity pieces. No new named characters -- Corren Halst and Danne Sok reused. Opens wave 23.

--- MCD-1102 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"The Garrison He Let Walk" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-garrison-he-let-walk.md), Bane Alias Chronicle LXXII, wave 24, closing wave 24. A garrison released under Bane's own amnesty terms re-arms and ambushes an unrelated Rebellion supply column weeks later, killing six -- the first entry to show a direct, specific cost of the mercy doctrine at strategic scale. Bane does not reverse the doctrine, states plainly to Corren Halst that the math was always going to cost something real eventually. No new named characters -- the former garrison captain is unnamed and does not appear on-page; Corren Halst reused.

--- MCD-1456 | category: kanja-alias-chronicle
"What He Couldn't Lift Twice" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/what-he-couldnt-lift-twice.md), Blue-Collar Titan Alias Chronicle XCIX, wave 33, closing the wave. The alias's first entry locating a genuine physical limit inside Kanja's own sustained exhaustion, extending 'The Watch That Forgot to Rest' (MCD-1189, where he imposed hard rotation caps on others) by finally applying that same rule to himself after three sleepless days leave his grip failing mid-lift. Deliberately framed around physical labor fatigue rather than tactical judgment, keeping it distinct from the same-shaped register already used for a different alias (Bane's MCD-1059). Reuses already-locked crew members Corren Halst and Danne Sok. No new named characters. Closes wave 33 (with MCD-1454 and MCD-1455).

# The White That Took the Map Away

*Locked canon, Batch 265, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1391`). Bane Alias Chronicle XCI, wave 31. New
environmental register -- a whiteout blizzard strips Sovereign Eyes' visual enhancement to nothing,
forcing a full-Trinity ambush defense to run entirely on sound, vibration, and Cadence Ruin.*

---

The storm hit two hours before the pass narrowed, and by the time the column reached the choke
point where the Directorate had been waiting for three days, there was no map left to read. Snow
came sideways hard enough to erase the column's own front rank from its rear, and the world had
gone the single flat color of nothing at all.

Sovereign Eyes had never failed him before. It failed him now, not through any defect in the gear
but through a plain, honest limit nobody had thought to test: there was nothing left in the white
for a predator's enhanced sight to find purchase on. Light-gathering meant nothing against a wall of
falling snow with no shape behind it. For the first time since the visor's earliest version, Bane
was, by every visual measure, as blind as anyone else on the mountain.

"Eyes are gone," he said to Corren Halst, flat, no alarm in it. "We fight this one on sound."

1	# The Last Night the Ravine Remembered
2	
3	*Locked canon, Batch 196, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-709`). Bane Alias Chronicle XLIV, wave 15 of the ten-wave sixth-through-fifteenth run. Not a territory Chronicle. Narrated in neutral third-person prose.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	The Directorate committed everything it had left built specifically to answer Bane to a single
8	night engagement at the Corrow ravine network — not the same ravine as the Black Trench, but close
9	enough in shape that the choice of ground was itself a message, a final, deliberate attempt to
10	answer the engagement that had made the name in the first place on ground built to echo it.
11	
12	Five companies. Two purpose-built Crawler variants, reinforced past anything fielded against the
13	Iron Bastard's own doctrine. A full night's planning built around every countermeasure eighteen
14	months of failure had taught them: no fresh-cut timber, no fog to hide movement in, no single choke
15	point a ravine-collapse tactic could exploit twice.
16	
17	Bane came in with the full Trinity engaged from the first contact, nothing held in reserve. Mafesto's
18	Kinetic Transfer System took the first Crawler's opening volley and grounded it clean through solid
19	rock this time, no marsh to rob the doctrine of its footing, redirected force enough to crack the
20	Crawler's forward plating on the return. Obsidian Malice discharged twice inside the first two
21	minutes — full charge both times, the two-year dormant-accumulation cycle long since built back to
22	capacity — each discharge timed to a moment when a full company's formation had closed tight enough
23	for the blast to matter and loose enough that his own position stayed clear of it. Onyx of Oblivion
24	moved through the space between discharges: Cadence Ruin unmaking a company commander's footing mid-
25	order, Veil Piercer finding the gap in a shield wall reinforced specifically to deny it, Whisper of
26	Shadows reading a Crawler's targeting cycle a half-second ahead of its trigger.
27	
28	The second Crawler nearly closed the fight the Directorate's planners had actually built it for —
29	armor plating layered to deny the resonance approach the Iron Bastard's own doctrine had made famous,
30	forcing Bane to abandon a single clean tactic and fight it the plain, grinding way instead, blade and
31	armor and raw strength against reinforced metal that gave ground only because he refused to stop
32	making it give ground.
33	
34	It ended at first light, five companies broken, both Crawlers disabled, the ravine network intact but
35	empty of anyone left standing to hold it. The engagement cost the column more than any fight since
36	the Black Trench itself — three wounded seriously enough to need the medic's full attention, nothing
37	fatal, everyone standing by dawn.
38	
39	"They built this whole night to answer the first ravine," the column's second said, surveying what
40	was left of five companies' worth of purpose-built countermeasures. "I don't think it answered
41	anything."
42	
43	"No. I don't think it was ever going to." Bane looked out at the ravine network, the same shape as
44	the one that had started all of it, eighteen months and a discarded name later. "Some things don't
45	get answered. They just get outlasted."
46	
47	---

# The Full Weight of the Trinity

*Locked canon, Batch 128, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-432`). Bane Alias Chronicle VIII. Rebellion era, age 19,
shortly after the Black Trench. Not a territory Chronicle. New standalone material — a detailed
armor-and-weapon combat showcase per Abad's craft instruction. Narrated in neutral third-person
prose. No new named characters.*

---

The garrison at the Kessic Overwatch had been built to survive exactly the kind of assault a rebel
force could normally mount against it — triple-walled, three interlocking kill-zones, a command
tower reinforced against anything short of a direct Titan-scale strike. It had not been built to
survive one man who had bonded a full Trinity two years before anyone in the garrison knew his name.

Bane went over the outer wall in full armor, and what followed was not a battle so much as a
demonstration of exactly how much a Trinity could do when nothing was held back.

Mafesto's Kinetic Transfer System absorbed the first kill-zone's volley crossfire directly into the
exoskeleton's plating rather than let momentum slow him — six simultaneous impacts converted to
stored charge in the time it took the garrison's second rank to loose their own volley, which found
him already past the zone entirely. Obsidian Malice discharged once against the inner gate, a
single strike concentrating two years of dormant charge into a blow that didn't so much break the
gate as make the question of its structural integrity briefly irrelevant. Onyx of Oblivion came free
of its sheath only once the gate was down, Cadence Ruin disrupting the coordinated rhythm of the
garrison's trained formation-fighting into six men each fighting alone instead of one unit fighting
together, Veil Piercer finding the gaps their own armor had never been designed to protect because no
attacker before him had ever needed to find them.

The command tower's captain met him on the top level with a loaded crossbow and the particular
calm of a man who had already accepted he wouldn't survive the next thirty seconds and had decided
to spend them well. He fired. Bane didn't dodge — Mafesto's plating absorbed the bolt's impact and
converted it, unremarkable, into the same stored charge everything else had become, and the captain
watched his last defense become fuel for the very thing it had been aimed at.

"How," the captain said. Not a question with an answer he expected to hear. Just the word, spoken
into a room he'd already accepted he wasn't leaving.

"Two years of preparation nobody outside my own crew knew was happening. A Trinity most of the
Directorate still doesn't believe is real, because believing it means admitting how unprepared every
garrison like this one actually is." Bane lowered Obsidian Malice, its cycle not yet fully spent.
"You built walls against an army. I'm not an army. I'm one man who spent two years making sure that
wouldn't matter."

The garrison surrendered within the hour, the captain among them — the Trinity's charge deliberately
left unspent rather than turned on men who no longer had anything left to fight with.

---

text:
# The Duel That Would Cost Nothing But Him

*Locked canon, Batch 276, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1425`). Bane Alias Chronicle XCV, wave 32. First deliberate
full-Trinity stand-down: a garrison commander's wager duel fought entirely with a plain blade, no
Onyx, Mafesto, or Obsidian Malice engaged, distinct from the peer-level duel of "The Fight He
Couldn't Walk Away From" (`MCD-476`).*

---

The commander sent the offer under a truce flag three days into a siege he already knew he'd lose:
single combat, himself against Bane, on open ground between the lines, weapons only, no tricks. If
the commander won, the column withdrew and the siege ended. If he lost, the garrison surrendered
whole, every soldier walking out alive.

"He knows he's beaten," Corren Halst said. "This is him choosing how many of his men die finding that
out."

"Then let him choose it cheap," Bane said, and sent back one condition of his own: no gear beyond the
blade at his hip. Onyx stayed sheathed and silent. Mafesto and Obsidian Malice stayed with the column.
Whatever happened on that ground would happen to him alone, on nothing but what Valen Sinisterblade
had spent years putting into his hands before any of the rest of it existed.

The commander was good — trained young, disciplined, patient in a way most of Bane's opponents
weren't, since most of them had never had reason to test a blade against him without also testing
whatever else came with the name. He opened cautious, reading for an opening that wasn't there yet,
and Bane gave him nothing to read: no myth, no reputation, just a stance and a breath and the
specific quiet Valen had spent a year drilling into him before he ever went into the Rebellion at all.

The fight ran long. Neither man rushed it. The commander's footwork was clean enough to hold even
ground for the better part of twenty minutes, testing angles, retreating when a line closed too
tight, conserving. Bane matched him breath for breath rather than force for force — not because he
couldn't have ended it faster with power in reserve, but because that reserve wasn't on the table
today, and the commander deserved a fight decided by what was actually there. It came down, in the
end, to who tired first and who noticed it soonest: the commander's guard dropped a fraction on his
back leg in the twenty-third minute, an old fatigue tell, and Bane's blade was at his throat before
the man had finished correcting it.

He didn't take the kill. He hadn't planned to.

"You held your ground a long time," Bane told him, lowering the blade. "That's not nothing. It's why
your men walk out standing instead of carried."

The commander, breathing hard, looked at the sheathed sword at Bane's hip rather than at his face.
"They tell stories about what you carry. Nobody tells stories about how you actually fight."

"They should," Bane said. "It's the only part of any of it that was ever mine to begin with."

The garrison marched out under its own colors an hour later, weapons surrendered, no further blood
spent on either side.

---

*Continuity notes (not narrative): first Bane entry to stage an entire engagement with the Trinity
completely stood down by his own choice rather than by malfunction, environmental limit, or tactical
withholding mid-fight (contrast the deliberate but partial Obsidian Malice restraint of "The Weight of
the Ones Who Didn't Run," `MCD-1113`) -- Onyx, Mafesto, and Obsidian Malice are not merely unused here,
they are explicitly kept out of the terms before the fight begins, isolating Kanja's own trained
swordsmanship (Valen Sinisterblade's training, `MCD-291`/`MCD-292`) as the sole deciding factor,
distinct from the peer-level duel of "The Fight He Couldn't Walk Away From" (`MCD-476`), which still
involved Onyx's Cadence Ruin and Veil Piercer. Extends the mercy-doctrine established across the run
(sparing the commander, honoring the wager's own terms in full) by tying it explicitly to a wager
that spares an entire garrison rather than one man. No new named characters -- the commander is
unnamed and one-scene; Corren Halst reused.*

# What the Enemy's Own Children Were Owed

*Locked canon, Batch 276, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1426`). Bane Alias Chronicle XCVI, wave 32, closing wave
32. First entry extending "the fear only works if it's true" (`MCD-431`) to the dependents of enemy
soldiers rather than to enemies, civilians, or captives themselves.*

---

The supply-chain campaign had done exactly what it was built to do: three weeks of quiet, deniable
sabotage (the same method that had starved the Threshbend depot into surrender, `MCD-700`) had cut
the garrison town's grain wagons off at the root, and the garrison itself was down to half-rations and
short tempers. It was working. Corren Halst said so with something close to satisfaction when the
column passed close enough to the town's outer quarter to see it.

What they saw first was children.

Not the garrison's — the garrison ate before anyone else did, same as any occupying force — but the
soldiers' own families, quartered in the civilian rows behind the walls, drawing on the same cut
supply the campaign had aimed at the men hunting Bane's column. A woman at a well told Danne Sok,
without knowing who was asking, that her husband hadn't eaten a full meal in nine days and neither had
their two children, and that she didn't blame anyone for the war, she just wanted it to stop taking
things from people who hadn't started it.

Bane had a wagon of captured grain, taken from the same garrison's own stores two days earlier, meant
to feed the column through the next stretch of road. He redirected half of it into the civilian
quarter that night, in the dark, no announcement, no name attached.

Corren Halst caught up with him before it finished. "You're feeding the families of the men who'll be
shooting at us again inside a month, once their supply line's patched."

"I'm feeding children whose fathers didn't ask them what side to be born on," Bane said. "The campaign
was never against them. If it starts costing them specifically, it's not pressure anymore, it's
punishment with worse aim than the garrison itself has."

"That's a distinction the garrison won't make."

"It's not their distinction to make. It's mine." He watched the last sack come off the wagon. "The
reputation only holds if it's actually true that I'm not the thing they're afraid I am. The day it
stops being true for someone just because they're standing on the wrong side of a wall, it stops being
true at all."

The woman from the well found the marked crates at her door the next morning and never learned who
left them, and never asked the column's escort — moving through at dawn, ordinary and unremarkable —
a single question about it.

---

*Continuity notes (not narrative): first entry to extend "the fear only works if it's true"
(`MCD-431`) to the families of enemy soldiers specifically, distinct from every prior mercy or aid
entry, which aided civilians, captives, or neutral parties but never dependents of the men actively
fighting him -- also the first entry to complicate the supply-chain-sabotage siege method itself
(`MCD-700`) by showing its unintended reach into noncombatants on the enemy's own side, without Bane
reversing or apologizing for the campaign, only correcting its edge. No new named characters -- the
woman and her family are unnamed; Corren Halst and Danne Sok reused. Closes wave 32 (with "The Tide
That Wrote the Deadline," `MCD-1424`, and "The Duel That Would Cost Nothing But Him," `MCD-1425`).*

*Locked canon, Batch 196, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-706`). Bane Alias Chronicle XLI, wave 14 of the ten-wave sixth-through-fifteenth run. Not a territory Chronicle. Narrated in neutral third-person prose.*

He told the settlement at Karrow's Bend that he would return before the season's first frost with
enough of the column to hold the pass against the Directorate reprisal everyone knew was coming for
having sheltered rebellion wounded. It was not an idle promise. It was the specific kind of assurance
the "Already-Finished Negotiation" reputation had trained people to trust completely — that if Bane
said a thing would happen, it had, in some sense, already happened, and the waiting was only for the
world to catch up to it.

He did not return before the frost. A crisis three provinces distant — a liberation operation that
could not wait and could not be delegated in time — held the column past the date he'd given, and by
the time word reached him that Karrow's Bend had been unable to wait any longer for a promise that
wasn't arriving, the reprisal had already come and gone.

cost: homes burned, four dead, a community that had trusted a specific date enough to stop preparing

Toran's own standing order held the whole three nights without him needing to invoke it by name:

# The Officer Who Wasn't Lying

*Locked canon, Batch 230, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1027`). Bane Alias Chronicle LIX, wave 20. Extends
`VB-060`'s "Already-Finished Negotiation" presence trait in reverse -- an opponent whose sincerity,
not deception, is what unsettles Bane. Not a territory Chronicle.*

---

The Directorate captain came alone, unarmed, in daylight, and said the thing Bane had heard a hundred
variations of from a hundred men trying to buy time, save their own skins, or set a trap: that he
wanted to defect.

Bane had spent years learning to hear the shape of a lie inside a sentence like that — the practiced
pause before the plea, the eyes that checked the treeline instead of his face, the offer that arrived
a half-second too eager. He listened for all of it now, out of habit more than expectation, and found
none of it. The captain's account of what had turned him — six months watching Scrip-Tether quotas
override medical triage in a border camp, one specific child's name he gave without being asked —
didn't have the shape of a story built to be believed. It had the shape of a man who'd simply stopped
being able to do the job.

"Already-finished negotiation" was Bane's own private name for what he did to rooms like this one,
the thing Callum Breck had once told him he did without seeming to try — arriving at a conclusion
somewhere the other man hadn't been invited and only announcing the result. It worked because most
men brought him something to see through. This one hadn't brought anything. He'd simply stood there,
plainly, and let himself be read, and there was nothing underneath the surface to find, which
unsettled Bane in a way no trap ever had.

"You're not lying," Bane said finally, and watched something in the captain's shoulders release that
had nothing to do with fear of being caught.

"No."

"That's the problem. I know exactly what to do with a man who's lying to me. I've never had to work
out what a defector who isn't costs the rest of you when your own side finds out he's gone."

He took the captain in — not on faith, not without six weeks of the same careful verification any
Directorate defector earned, Danne Sok's own network confirming every claim the man made piece by
piece — but he took him in having already believed him from the first sentence, which was the part
that stayed with him longer than the verification did. Every alias he'd built, every reputation he'd
let the Directorate write for him, ran on being unreadable. He hadn't built anything for being the one
doing the reading of a man with nothing to hide, and he suspected, walking away from that first
conversation, that he was going to need it more often than the years ahead of him would be
comfortable with.

---

*Continuity notes (not narrative): the first entry to test `VB-060`'s presence trait against genuine
sincerity rather than deception -- distinct from every prior tribunal, interrogation, or negotiation
entry, where Bane reads through a performance. No new named characters -- Danne Sok and Callum Breck
referenced consistently with their already-locked roles; the defecting captain is deliberately left
unnamed. Second entry in wave 20.*

vibration of coordinated footsteps through the riverbed itself, picking apart an attempted pincer

Obsidian Malice was the one piece of the Trinity Bane held back from its usual answer. A full
discharge released into open water, with forty of his own people still fording it, could have hurt
more of them than the enemy — so when the moment came that called for it, he raised the blade clear
of the surface and released the charge upward and outward instead, a controlled arc over the water
rather than through it, taking the last organized resistance on the bank without ever letting the
current carry the current.

they closed rather than in the middle of a clash where a misjudged blast radius would have mattered;

# The Story That Outran Him

*Locked canon, Batch 276, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1432`). Bane Alias Chronicle CII, wave 34, closing wave
34 and this three-wave run. Extends the legend-drift theme of "The Song They Sang Without Knowing
Whose It Was" (`MCD-1108`) beyond his own people into an unverifiable, uncontrolled echo reaching a
place he has never been.*

---

The trader mentioned it the way he mentioned everything else that came through his wagon — a small
"No," Bane said.

"You have no way to reach them. No way to confirm what they're actually doing in your name, whether
it's decent or whether it's the kind of thing that gets people killed for a story that isn't even
true."

"No," Bane said again, and that was the whole of it, because there wasn't a version of the fact that
changed with more thinking about it. The song at the waystation, the rumor in the market town, the
impersonators wearing his shape for profit — all of that had been close enough to reach, close enough
to correct or confirm or at least witness. This wasn't. This was the name doing something on its own,
three provinces past the edge of anywhere he could follow it, built off a story a trader had told a
trader had told a trader, accurate in no way he could verify and inaccurate in no way he could
correct.

Efa Gol found him still turning it over that evening. "You look like a man who just found out he owes
money somewhere he's never been."

"Worse," Bane said. "I look like a man who found out something with my name on it is making decisions
I'll never get a vote in, for people I'll never meet, based on a version of events that's already three
tellings removed from anything that actually happened." He shook his head slowly. "The song at the
waystation, I could have stopped if I'd wanted to. This one doesn't need me at all anymore. It just
needed to start."

"Does that scare you?"

text:
# The Garrison He Let Walk

*Locked canon, Batch 254, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1102`). Bane Alias Chronicle LXXII, wave 24, closing wave
24. A garrison released under Bane's own amnesty ethic re-arms and ambushes an unrelated Rebellion
column weeks later -- the first entry to show a direct, specific cost of the mercy doctrine at
strategic scale.*

---

The garrison at Kessic Overwatch had surrendered clean six weeks earlier — no tricks, no staged
wounded, an honest capitulation Bane had accepted on the same terms he always offered: lay down arms,
walk free, never take them up again against the rebellion. Most who took that deal kept it. Some
didn't have anywhere else to go and drifted back into whatever work had fed them before the war.

The garrison's former captain went back to his commission inside three weeks. He led the ambush that
hit a Rebellion supply column forty miles east, one Bane's own people had never touched, killing six
before the column's escort drove them off.

Bane heard it secondhand, three days after it happened, from a runner who hadn't known the ambush
commander's name meant anything to him specifically.

He didn't call a council. He didn't announce a change in policy. He found Corren Halst at the edge of
camp that night and said it plainly, the way he said most things that actually cost him something.

"Six people are dead who wouldn't be if I'd held that garrison instead of releasing it."

"You couldn't have known he'd break the terms."

"That's not the same as not owing the cost. I knew when I started doing this that some of the people
I let walk would use it to hurt someone else eventually. I did it anyway because the alternative was
holding or killing people who hadn't done anything to earn either, on the chance that one of them
might. I still think that's right. I'm not going to pretend six people paid nothing for me thinking
it."

"You're not going to stop offering the terms."

"No." Bane looked out at the dark beyond the fire line, where the news had come from. "The math
doesn't change because it cost something real this time. It was always going to, eventually. I just
hadn't had to sit with it yet."

Halst didn't argue him out of the doctrine, and didn't try to talk him into feeling better about it
either. He sat with him instead, until the fire burned down, and neither of them said anything else
about it that night.

---

*Continuity notes (not narrative): first entry to dramatize a direct, specific cost of Bane's
amnesty/mercy doctrine at strategic scale -- distinct from "The Promise He Couldn't Keep" (`MCD-706`,
a broken promise, not a granted mercy) and "The Surrender That Wasn't One" (`MCD-910`, a fake
surrender exposed and defeated in the moment, not a genuine amnesty abused later). The doctrine is
explicitly not reversed. No new named characters -- the former garrison captain is unnamed and does
not appear on-page; Corren Halst reused. Closes wave 24.*

7:The leg had been giving her trouble since long before anyone else noticed, and by the time Corren Halst finally said something about it, she'd already worked out exactly how she wanted the conversation to go.
9:"It's not the fighting that's the problem," she told Kanja, testing her weight against the old dock injury that flared worse every winter now. "It's the ladders. Front-line tunnel work means ladders, and ladders mean a leg that doesn't always answer when I need it to."
13:"Longer than I should have. I kept telling myself it wasn't bad enough yet to matter." She held his gaze rather than looking away from the admission. "It's bad enough now. I'm not asking you to fix it. I'm telling you because pretending otherwise gets someone hurt on a rotation I shouldn't still be running."
15:It would have been easy, and not without precedent elsewhere in the crew's history, to treat this as a problem requiring reassurance -- to insist she could still manage, to quietly redesign rotations around her rather than name the change plainly. Kanja didn't reach for that instinct.
23:Corren Halst was quiet for a moment, turning the offer over with the same care she gave any structural read.
25:"You turned down a permanent seat on the workers' council," she said finally. "Kept only the advisory chair, so the authority wouldn't sit with you by default just because you'd earned it once."
31:"That's exactly what it is." Kanja held out a hand, and she took it, the handshake settling something neither of them needed to say aloud. "I've had eight decades of people trying to make me the exception to every rule this crew runs on. You don't get to be the exception either, not even the kind that quietly steps aside before anyone asks her to. You're too good at this to let a ladder decide where your knowledge stops mattering."
33:Word of the new arrangement reached Danne Sok by the following morning, and she found Corren Halst already at the training hall, a fresh line of recruits waiting for their first lesson.
35:"How does the chair feel?" Danne Sok asked.
37:"Feels like the same work I've always done," Corren Halst said, "just finally admitted out loud as the actual work, instead of something I was quietly doing around the edges of a job my leg was never going to let me keep pretending I still had."

=== the-pass-above-the-orphan-road.md ===
9:The pass was narrow, switchbacked, and cold in a way none of the coastal engagements had ever been, wind cutting sideways off exposed rock with nothing but a thin caravan line of children and handlers strung along it for half a mile. Corren Halst walked the column's spine, keeping the pace even so no single stretch was ever undefended for long. Pell Ostra had rigged nothing explosive this time — the risk of rockfall onto the column itself ruled it out — and instead laid quiet deadfall traps along the only two approach lines a raiding party could use without exposing themselves on open scree.
11:They came from above at the pass's narrowest point, eleven men working ropes down a face they'd clearly scouted in advance. Kanja read the rock face before the first rope even went taut — the same instinctive Rexmar-Mar sense for terrain and intent that had carried him through every engagement long before any gear existed to help it, sharpened now by the Sovereign Eyes' low, patient glow picking out handholds and breath-sound against wind that should have hidden everything. The Forge-Coat's plating and the Ironfall Boots' grounded, impact-sole stance let him catch the first man's dropped grapple and throw the force back up the line through his own braced weight, snapping two ropes clean before their owners had descended twenty feet; one leveraged strike from the Ironhand Gauntlets — trained technique through riveted plate, nothing more — sheared rock low and angled, sending a controlled slide across the only approach still open rather than into the column itself. Kanja closed the last three personally, the Rexmar Machete doing the rest: an excellent blade in a swordsman's hands, footwork built for balance on a slope no ordinary fighter could hold, every strike disarming, the Smoke System's low haze covering his approach so none of the three saw him coming until it was already over.
13:Not one child on that caravan saw more than distant shapes moving fast against grey stone. They reached the resettlement house by dusk, cold and tired and entirely unaware how close the pass had come to going differently, and Corren Halst logged the engagement afterward under a line of her own: eleven turned back, zero children touched, the only number that had ever mattered to this particular job.
17:*Continuity notes (not narrative): the sub-series' first detailed combat showcase set on a high mountain pass, a genuinely new environmental register for Captain distinct from every prior setting (causeway `MCD-396`, fortified strongpoint `MCD-461`, safehouse `MCD-507`, siege line `MCD-558`, fishing-village pier `MCD-1058`, civic plaza `MCD-1091`), and the first to put the full seven-piece Long-Mask-era gear system's terrain/melee/perception/concealment functions on the page together inside the Captain sub-series specifically -- Mafesto, Obsidian Malice, and Onyx of Oblivion (including Whisper of Shadows) do not and cannot appear here, consistent with the Trinity's already-locked age-30 vault surrender (`MCD-246`) for the entire Long Mask era this entry is set within. No new named characters -- Corren Halst, Pell Ostra, and Kanja all reused; the resettlement handlers, the forty-one children, and the eleven raiders are deliberately unnamed. First entry, wave 23.*

=== five-years-as-promised.md ===
3:*Locked canon, Batch 264, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1379`). Captain Alias Chronicle LXXIX, wave 27. Direct payoff: Kanja asks Corren Halst the succession question again, exactly as promised five years before.*
7:Kanja remembered the date the way he remembered every casualty-list name he'd ever checked himself — not because he'd marked it anywhere, but because some promises simply didn't need a ledger to stay counted. Five years, almost to the week, since Garren Hask's notebook had come out of hiding and Corren Halst had asked him to wait before naming her anything.
9:He found her checking rigging on the Second Chance, not the Receipt, the way she always did when she wanted a quiet hour before whatever came next. He didn't announce the question. He just sat down on the rail beside her and let her get there herself.
11:"Five years," she said, not looking up from the line in her hands.
15:She finished the knot before she answered, which he'd learned by now meant she wasn't stalling — she simply didn't do anything halfway, not even a conversation this size. "I have thought about it. Longer than five years, if I'm honest — I started actually turning it over the week after Hask asked, not the week before you came to collect the answer." She set the rope down. "And I don't think the answer's as simple as yes or no. I think that's the mistake in the question itself."
19:"Whether one person taking over for you is even the right shape for what this has become. You built something that runs on Halst leading a rescue while you're gone, and Hask running the ledger while his own heart gives out, and Efa Gol training a second set of hands so the count stays honest after hers slow down. That's not one successor waiting in the wings. That's an institution that's already been quietly training itself not to need any single person, including you. I don't think I should be the answer. I think I should help build whatever the real answer turns out to be."
23:*Continuity notes (not narrative): the direct, long-flagged payoff to "The Notebook Garren Hask Finally Opened" (`MCD-1090`, wave 21) -- Corren Halst's five-year promise, paid off on schedule rather than accelerated or forgotten, and deliberately complicated rather than resolved into a simple yes. References, as her own evidence, the self-sufficiency pattern this run has been quietly building across waves 22-26 ("The Command He Left Behind," `MCD-1364`; Hask's mortality entries, `MCD-1089`/`1090`; Efa Gol's own succession-adjacent training, `MCD-1373`), tying the wave's opener directly to material built earlier in this same run. No new named characters -- Corren Halst and Kanja reused. First entry, wave 27.*

=== what-he-couldnt-lift-twice.md ===
3:*Locked canon, Batch 279, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1456`). Blue-Collar Titan Alias Chronicle XCIX, wave 33, closing the wave. The alias's first entry making Kanja himself subject to his own established fatigue rule rather than the one imposing it on others.*
7:His arms told him first, a fine tremor he mistook for cold until he noticed the tunnel around him was warm enough to sweat in. He'd been three days without real sleep, running triage between the frost repairs, the dry well, and a support timber that had started groaning somewhere he hadn't gotten to yet, and it was the fourth crisis in as many days that finally found the seam in him rather than in the rock.
11:"Set it down," Corren Halst said, already at his shoulder, voice flat in the way that meant she wasn't asking.
15:"You had it. For half a second there, you didn't." She didn't reach for the beam herself, didn't try to wrestle it from him -- she knew better than that. She simply stood where he could see her and waited, and it was Danne Sok arriving a moment later, reading the same tremor in his forearms that Corren Halst had already caught, who finally said the thing that landed.
17:"You made a rule after the night crew nearly lost two men to exhaustion nobody caught in time," Danne Sok said. "You wrote it into how this crew runs. You didn't write an exception into it for yourself."
23:"Knowing it and living under it aren't the same thing, and you of all people should know that better than anyone." Corren Halst nodded toward the tunnel mouth. "Three days. You'd have pulled anyone else off rotation after one."
25:It would have been easy to argue that he wasn't like anyone else on the rotation -- that his own capacity ran further before it broke, that the crises hadn't waited for him to finish resting between them, that someone still needed to be the one holding all four problems in his head at once. None of it would have been dishonest. All of it would have been exactly the kind of exception he'd refused to grant anyone else, on exactly the grounds he'd refused to accept from them.
31:"How does it feel," Danne Sok asked, "being the exception you finally didn't make for yourself?"
37:*Continuity notes (not narrative): the alias's first entry locating a genuine physical limit inside Kanja's own sustained exhaustion, extending "The Watch That Forgot to Rest" (`MCD-1189`, where he imposed hard rotation caps on others) by finally applying that same rule to himself for the first time -- distinct from the structural-failure limit of `MCD-485` and the technical-mistake register of `MCD-665`, since here the limit is bodily rather than a misjudgment of stone. Deliberately framed around physical labor fatigue (a failing grip mid-lift) rather than tactical judgment, keeping it distinct from the same-shaped register already used for a different alias (Bane's `MCD-1059`). Reuses already-locked crew members Corren Halst and Danne Sok (both she/her). No new named characters. Closes wave 33 (with "The Well That Went Dry," `MCD-1454`, and "The Hand He Rebuilt to Hold a Tool," `MCD-1455`).*

=== the-machine-that-dug-toward-them.md ===
7:The vibration reached Danne Sok's palm before it reached her ears, a slow, rhythmic grinding through the rock that didn't match any collapse she'd ever felt and didn't match any tool the crew owned either.
9:"That's not settling," she said, already backing away from the gallery wall. "That's coming."
11:Kanja pressed both hands flat against the stone and held them there through a dozen cycles of the grinding before he understood what he was reading. Not men digging. A machine -- a Directorate boring engine, iron-toothed and steam-driven, cutting a straight line through solid rock toward the civilian shelter gallery three hundred paces east, indifferent to the workers sleeping in it because nothing riding inside it could hear them scream.
15:There was no negotiating with it and no diverting it the way he'd diverted heat or gas -- a machine that size didn't care about a rerouted gallery, and by the time it broke through to the shelter there would be nothing left to reroute around. Mafesto's kinetic transfer read the grinding itself, mapping the engine's cutting head against the vibration pattern until Kanja had its exact position and speed to within a body-length, close enough to intercept it before it reached the shelter's outer wall rather than after.
19:The four Directorate engineers riding its rear compartment came out fighting, and Onyx of Oblivion's Cadence Ruin dropped the first two before they cleared the hatch; Veil Piercer caught the third reaching for a lever that would have reversed the stalled engine straight back through its own crew. The fourth surrendered with his hands already in the air, staring at the seized machine rather than at the man who'd stopped it.
23:"Because I know exactly what that drive shaft is worth to build, and exactly what it costs to fix." Kanja knelt beside the stilled engine, running a palm along its housing the way he'd have checked any machine he intended to repair rather than salvage. "Breaking things is easy. Knowing precisely how little you actually need to break to stop them is the whole trade."
25:Danne Sok caught up to him a few minutes later, looking at the seized engine with something between admiration and disbelief. "You fought a machine like it was a man you were trying not to kill."

# The Rotation Corren Halst Finally Took

*Locked canon, Batch 279, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1459`); corrected Batch 320, 2026-10-01 (Corren Halst
and Danne Sok reconciled to he/him, matching the clear majority usage across the corpus and the
same resolution already applied to Maret Vos and Dol Maren, Batch 226). Blue-Collar Titan Alias
Chronicle CII, wave 34, closing the wave. A graceful institutional handoff extended to one of
Kanja's own founding crew for the first time, mirroring his own declined permanent council seat.*

---

The leg had been giving him trouble since long before anyone else noticed, and by the time Corren Halst finally said something about it, he'd already worked out exactly how he wanted the conversation to go.

"It's not the fighting that's the problem," he told Kanja, testing his weight against the old dock injury that flared worse every winter now. "It's the ladders. Front-line tunnel work means ladders, and ladders mean a leg that doesn't always answer when I need it to."

"How long have you been managing around it instead of telling anyone?"

"Longer than I should have. I kept telling myself it wasn't bad enough yet to matter." He held Kanja's gaze rather than looking away from the admission. "It's bad enough now. I'm not asking you to fix it. I'm telling you because pretending otherwise gets someone hurt on a rotation I shouldn't still be running."

It would have been easy, and not without precedent elsewhere in the crew's history, to treat this as a problem requiring reassurance -- to insist he could still manage, to quietly redesign rotations around him rather than name the change plainly. Kanja didn't reach for that instinct.

"Then you're off front-line rotation," he said. "Not out of the crew. Off the ladders."

"That's the easy half of the sentence. What's the rest of it?"

"The rest is that you've spent this entire war reading a crisis faster than almost anyone I've ever worked beside, and that doesn't stop mattering just because your leg won't take a ladder anymore." Kanja considered the training hall down the corridor, still bearing the marks of the safety-certification classes he'd started years before. "Training. Every new recruit who comes through that hall learns to read a tunnel from you before they ever touch a tool. Nobody on this crew reads faster or teaches straighter."

Corren Halst was quiet for a moment, turning the offer over with the same care he gave any structural read.

"You turned down a permanent seat on the workers' council," he said finally. "Kept only the advisory chair, so the authority wouldn't sit with you by default just because you'd earned it once."

"I remember."

"This is the same shape, isn't it. You're not retiring me. You're moving the thing I'm actually best at somewhere my leg can't disqualify me from it."

"That's exactly what it is." Kanja held out a hand, and he took it, the handshake settling something neither of them needed to say aloud. "I've had eight decades of people trying to make me the exception to every rule this crew runs on. You don't get to be the exception either, not even the kind that quietly steps aside before anyone asks him to. You're too good at this to let a ladder decide where your knowledge stops mattering."

Word of the new arrangement reached Danne Sok by the following morning, and he found Corren Halst already at the training hall, a fresh line of recruits waiting for their first lesson.

"How does the chair feel?" Danne Sok asked.

"Feels like the same work I've always done," Corren Halst said, "just finally admitted out loud as the actual work, instead of something I was quietly doing around the edges of a job my leg was never going to let me keep pretending I still had."

---

4	territory Chronicle. Narrated in neutral third-person prose.*

7	
8	Eight months after the surrender, Garren Hask called the dispute council back into session the way
9	he'd promised he would — once the peace had settled enough, he'd said, to see clearly what the coast
10	actually needed from a crew that no longer had an enemy telling it what to be. Nobody had forced the
11	question in the meantime. It had simply sat there, unresolved, while the coast rebuilt around them
12	and the crew kept doing the ordinary work of a crew without anyone deciding whether it was still
13	supposed to.
14	
15	"We're not going to answer all of it today," Hask said, laying a blank ledger page on the table
16	instead of a finished one. "I don't think we're capable of that, and I don't think pretending
17	otherwise would serve anybody. But eight months is long enough to know a few things for certain, and
18	I'd rather write down what's certain than keep waiting for the parts that aren't."
19	
20	Corren Halst went first, the way she usually did now. "Nobody's here because a war is making them
21	stay. That's been true for months and nobody's left. That's not nothing."
22	
23	"Say it as a rule, then," Efa Gol said. "Not a feeling. A rule somebody new can read."
24	
25	So they wrote it as a rule. Membership was chosen, not assigned, and stayed chosen — anyone could
26	leave at any time, for any reason or none, owing no explanation to the ledger or the council or to
27	Kanja personally, the same standing the crew had already extended to Maret Vos months before the war
28	even ended. The dispute council's authority stood on its own, independent of any war that had once
29	made it necessary, empowered to settle disputes, admit new members, and govern the ship's affairs
30	whether or not there was ever another enemy to justify it. And Kanja sat in council as one voting
31	seat among five, his word carrying no more formal weight than Hask's or Breck's or Halst's, a
32	standing the council had been training itself toward for years before it ever needed writing down.
33	
34	"That's three things," Callum Breck said, reading it back. "There's a fourth nobody's said yet."
35	
36	Kanja didn't wait for someone else to raise it. "What happens when the ones who remember why we
37	started this are gone, and I'm the only one left who was there." He said it plainly, the way he'd
38	learned to say the things that didn't have comfortable answers. "I don't have that one. I told you
39	that already, at the last meeting. I still don't have it."
40	
41	"Then leave it blank," Hask said, and did — a fourth line on the page, headed and dated, with
42	nothing written under it. "Not every question gets an answer the day you're brave enough to ask it.
43	Some of them just get a place held for when you're ready."
44	
45	The council signed the first three lines and left the fourth exactly as blank as Hask had made it,

2	
3	*Locked canon, Batch 251, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1091`). Captain Alias Chronicle LXIII, wave 21, closing

14	alias but to "the crew of Pier Nine, under whatever name they answer to now" -- a district
15	administrator needed protection for a grain distribution three days off, the granaries themselves

17	settlement had suffered a season before, and this time offering coin for it, the first payment the
18	Trust had ever formally offered the crew for anything.
19	
20	Corren Halst read it twice before she'd say a word. "We fought them for twelve years. Now they want to
21	pay us to guard their own storehouses."
22	
23	"They want to pay us to make sure their storehouses reach people who'll starve without them," Kanja
24	said. "That's not the same debt. I'm not defending the Trust. I'm feeding whoever's standing in that
25	line, and I don't see why the coin changes what we'd already be doing for free."
26	
27	Efa Gol settled it the way she settled most things, with a number. "Twelve hundred people on that
28	distribution list. Take the coin. Feed twelve hundred people. Argue about what it means after."
29	
30	The raiders came at midday, when the line was longest and the plaza most crowded -- eight men who'd
31	planned to hit the granary doors in the crush and vanish into the same crowd they'd be robbing, betting
32	correctly that the administrator's own thin garrison wouldn't risk firing into that many bystanders.
33	What they hadn't planned for was Kanja's own eye sweeping the packed plaza before the first sack was
34	even touched, the same instinctive Rexmar-Mar reading that had never needed anything but his own
35	trained attention to find a lie in a crowd, picking past eight ordinary postures and eight
36	deliberately ordinary faces to the one shared tell none of them could fully hide -- the way each
37	man's attention kept snapping back to the same two exits, over and over, the way no one waiting
38	patiently in a food line ever does. Kanja had three of them marked before the first hand reached a
39	granary latch.
40	
41	He fought it the way the gear built after the Trinity's surrender had been designed to fight anywhere
42	people who weren't soldiers stood too close to the danger. The Forge-Coat and Ironfall Boots took the
43	first raider's drawn blade not with a strike but a redirect -- the Boots' grounding function turning
44	Kanja's own planted stance into an anchor, the coat's plating guiding the man's committed lunge wide
45	into an empty stretch of plaza stone instead of the woman he'd been aiming past, trained technique and
46	engineered gear doing together what neither could alone. The Ironhand Gauntlets answered the other
47	three in short, precisely placed strikes rather than one sweeping blow -- leverage through riveted
48	plate, no discharge, no burst, just a fist landing exactly as hard as it needed to and no harder --
49	dropping each of the marked men where he stood without the wider commotion that would have scattered
50	the crowd into a panic that killed more people than the raid itself ever could have. Kanja closed the
51	last two exits personally, reading the plaza's own uneven cobblestones under a dead sprint on instinct
52	alone and landing between the fleeing men and the alley they'd banked on, the Rexmar Machete doing the
53	rest -- every blow disarming rather than killing, exactly the way his own trained swordsmanship always
54	aimed it.

57	white-faced and clearly expecting to have to apologize for something, found instead that the
58	distribution had barely paused -- Callum Breck had kept the queue moving with silent hand-signals

63	everything, and logged it under a line she wrote herself: not payment for service to the Trust, but

reconciled to he/him, matching `CC-158`). Captain Alias Chronicle LXXIX, wave 27. Direct payoff: Kanja asks Corren Halst the succession question again, exactly as promised five years before.*

---

Kanja remembered the date the way he remembered every casualty-list name he'd ever checked himself — not because he'd marked it anywhere, but because some promises simply didn't need a ledger to stay counted. Five years, almost to the week, since Garren Hask's notebook had come out of hiding and Corren Halst had asked him to wait before naming him anything.

He found Halst checking rigging on the Second Chance, not the Receipt, the way he always did when he wanted a quiet hour before whatever came next. He didn't announce the question. He just sat down on the rail beside him and let him get there himself.

"Five years," Halst said, not looking up from the line in his hands.

"Five years," Kanja agreed. "You said ask you again once you'd actually thought about it instead of reacting to Hask nearly dying in front of us. I'm asking."

He finished the knot before he answered, which Kanja had learned by now meant he wasn't stalling — he simply didn't do anything halfway, not even a conversation this size. "I have thought about it. Longer than five years, if I'm honest — I started actually turning it over the week after Hask asked, not the week before you came to collect the answer." He set the rope down. "And I don't think the answer's as simple as yes or no. I think that's the mistake in the question itself."

"Then tell me what the question should have been."

"Whether one person taking over for you is even the right shape for what this has become. You built something that runs on Halst leading a rescue while you're gone, and Hask running the ledger while his own heart gives out, and Efa Gol training a second set of hands so the count stays honest after hers slow down. That's not one successor waiting in the wings. That's an institution that's already been quietly training itself not to need any single person, including you. I don't think I should be the answer. I think I should help build whatever the real answer turns out to be."

---

1	# What He Couldn't Lift Twice
2	
3	*Locked canon, Batch 279, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1456`). Blue-Collar Titan Alias Chronicle XCIX, wave 33, closing the wave. The alias's first entry making Kanja himself subject to his own established fatigue rule rather than the one imposing it on others.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	His arms told him first, a fine tremor he mistook for cold until he noticed the tunnel around him was warm enough to sweat in. He'd been three days without real sleep, running triage between the frost repairs, the dry well, and a support timber that had started groaning somewhere he hadn't gotten to yet, and it was the fourth crisis in as many days that finally found the seam in him rather than in the rock.
8	
9	The beam went up on the first lift clean enough. It was the second lift -- shifting it six inches to seat properly against the new post -- that his grip failed on, just for a half-second, just long enough for the beam to drop back half an inch before he caught it again.
10	
11	"Set it down," Corren Halst said, already at his shoulder, voice flat in the way that meant she wasn't asking.
12	
13	"I've got it."
14	
15	"You had it. For half a second there, you didn't." She didn't reach for the beam herself, didn't try to wrestle it from him -- she knew better than that. She simply stood where he could see her and waited, and it was Danne Sok arriving a moment later, reading the same tremor in his forearms that Corren Halst had already caught, who finally said the thing that landed.
16	
17	"You made a rule after the night crew nearly lost two men to exhaustion nobody caught in time," Danne Sok said. "You wrote it into how this crew runs. You didn't write an exception into it for yourself."
18	
19	Kanja set the beam down, properly this time, and stood with both hands braced against the post for a moment longer than the work required.
20	
21	"I know the rule," he said.
22	
23	"Knowing it and living under it aren't the same thing, and you of all people should know that better than anyone." Corren Halst nodded toward the tunnel mouth. "Three days. You'd have pulled anyone else off rotation after one."
24	
25	It would have been easy to argue that he wasn't like anyone else on the rotation -- that his own capacity ran further before it broke, that the crises hadn't waited for him to finish resting between them, that someone still needed to be the one holding all four problems in his head at once. None of it would have been dishonest. All of it would have been exactly the kind of exception he'd refused to grant anyone else, on exactly the grounds he'd refused to accept from them.
26	
27	"You're right," he said instead. "Log it the same as you'd log anyone else. I'm off rotation until the rest catches up to the rule."
28	
29	He slept nine hours, the longest unbroken stretch since the frost had first started cracking timber, and returned to find the beam properly seated and the support timber's groan already traced and fixed by a crew that hadn't needed him standing over it to manage without him.
30	
31	"How does it feel," Danne Sok asked, "being the exception you finally didn't make for yourself?"
32	
33	"Honestly? It feels like I should have written the rule that way from the start." Kanja checked the newly seated beam with both hands, steady now, and found nothing wrong with it. "A rule that only binds everyone but the man who wrote it was never actually a safety rule. It was just an order with better manners."
34	
35	---
36	
37	*Continuity notes (not narrative): the alias's first entry locating a genuine physical limit inside Kanja's own sustained exhaustion, extending "The Watch That Forgot to Rest" (`MCD-1189`, where he imposed hard rotation caps on others) by finally applying that same rule to himself for the first time -- distinct from the structural-failure limit of `MCD-485` and the technical-mistake register of `MCD-665`, since here the limit is bodily rather than a misjudgment of stone. Deliberately framed around physical labor fatigue (a failing grip mid-lift) rather than tactical judgment, keeping it distinct from the same-shaped register already used for a different alias (Bane's `MCD-1059`). Reuses already-locked crew members Corren Halst and Danne Sok (both she/her). No new named characters. Closes wave 33 (with "The Well That Went Dry," `MCD-1454`, and "The Hand He Rebuilt to Hold a Tool," `MCD-1455`).*

2	
3	*Locked canon, Batch 268, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1400`). Blue-Collar Titan Alias Chronicle XCI, wave 31, opening the wave. The alias's first mechanized-siege-engine combat showcase -- a Directorate boring engine driven as a weapon in its own right, not a trap or a hazard.*

9	"That's not settling," she said, already backing away from the gallery wall. "That's coming."

11	Kanja pressed both hands flat against the stone and held them there through a dozen cycles of the grinding before he understood what he was reading. Not men digging. A machine -- a Directorate boring engine, iron-toothed and steam-driven, cutting a straight line through solid rock toward the civilian shelter gallery three hundred paces east, indifferent to the workers sleeping in it because nothing riding inside it could hear them scream.
12

# The Day the Whole Founding Crew Sat Down Together

*Locked canon, Batch 264, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1389`). Captain Alias Chronicle LXXXIX, wave 30. A warm, conflict-free founding-anniversary gathering, the sub-series' fullest celebratory entry.*

---

Nobody planned it as a formal occasion, which was, everyone agreed afterward, exactly why it worked. Efa Gol simply noted, checking a date against the ledger for an unrelated reason, that it had been exactly that many years since the morning after Iron Shallows, when Garren Hask had first called a young man fresh off a battle he barely believed he'd survived something other than the alias the Directorate had already begun writing into its files. She said it out loud at the evening meal, more observation than announcement, and somehow by the following week half the crew's history was sitting at the same long table without anyone having sent a single formal invitation.

Corren Halst came, between her rotating-chair duties, still carrying the same steady bearing that had once led a split engagement without needing him in the room. Callum Breck came with the trainee he'd taught the shore-watch craft to, proud in a way he'd never have shown before Ghost Harbor taught him a different kind of confidence. Garren Hask, slower now but stubbornly present, brought the notebook that had started this whole run of years, and the ledger's new keeper beside him, the same person who'd once sounded out letters under Kanja's patient finger. Efa Gol sat beside Mira, twenty now and fully, unhurriedly herself. Danne Sok's daughter came in off a real posting to tell stories that made the newer hands laugh. Maret Vos came too, quietly, the way he did most things, having chosen this a second time and never once regretted saying so out loud.

Pell Ostra told the story of the prank she'd spent a year planning, again, exaggerated further each time she told it. Sera came down from her hall for the evening, healer's satchel left behind for once, just a daughter among the people who'd raised her alongside her own father.

Kanja said little most of the night, content to let the table run itself the way the whole crew had learned to. When someone finally asked him to speak, he didn't reach for anything grand.

"I've had a lot of names," he said. "This is the only one any of you ever gave me for free."

---

*Continuity notes (not narrative): the sub-series' fullest reunion entry, gathering nearly every recurring named figure across the full run -- Corren Halst, Callum Breck, Garren Hask, Efa Gol, Mira, Danne Sok's daughter (`MCD-1002`), Maret Vos, Pell Ostra, and Sera -- in one conflict-free celebratory scene, deliberately distinct from the wedding (`MCD-919`), the toast (`MCD-463`), and the crew-wedding entry from the fourth Alias Chronicle wave. No new named characters. Second entry, wave 30.*
