# The Man He Let Walk Away

*Locked canon, Batch 268, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1402`). Blue-Collar Titan Alias Chronicle XCIII, wave 31, closing the wave. A former-enemy reconciliation entry -- the Trust combat engineer spared in "The Engineer Who Fought Like One" returns years later, no longer an adversary.*

---

Kanja recognized the walk before he recognized the face -- a man crossing the plaza the way a structural engineer always crossed open ground, reading its load lines out of old habit, the same careful contour-following gait he'd matched stride for stride in a narrow gallery years before neither of them meant to end that fight as friends.

"I told them the tunnel held," the man said, stopping an arm's length away. "That was true, as far as it went. I didn't tell them why I believed it."

"You didn't have to." Kanja set down the level he'd been using and studied him properly for the first time since the duel that had ended in a stalemate neither of them finished. "You look like a man who's spent the years since building things instead of defending them."

"Mostly. The war left half my own district's infrastructure in worse condition than anything I ever tried to break of yours." The engineer glanced toward the plaza's new well, the guild hall down the street, the visible evidence of thirty-odd Chronicles' worth of work. "I came to ask something I wouldn't have believed myself capable of asking, back when we were choosing ground to fight on instead of ground to build on. I want your crew's help. Not the alias's reputation -- your actual people, the ones who know what they're doing."

It would have been easy, and not unreasonable, to hear a request like that as an opening for suspicion -- a former enemy engineer seeking access to the crew that had out-built and outfought his own side for the length of a siege. Kanja didn't reach for that reading. The man across from him had chosen not to finish a fight he could plausibly have won, on the strength of nothing but recognizing honest craft in an opponent; that debt, unlike most owed from the war, had already been repaid in full the moment the blade came down.

"You'll get the same crew, and the same standards, as anyone else who's asked," Kanja said. "No favor for old respect. Just the actual work, done the way it's supposed to be done."

"That's the only answer that would've made me trust it," the engineer said, something close to relief in it. "I spent that whole fight learning you don't do things the easy way when the honest way is available. I was hoping that hadn't changed."

They shook on it in the open plaza, two men who'd once measured each other's worth in a narrow gallery with a blade half an inch from a killing stroke, now measuring a joint repair timeline instead. Danne Sok, watching from the guild hall steps, didn't need the story explained to her twice.

"That's the same one," she said. "The engineer who nearly had you."

"He didn't nearly have me. We nearly had each other, and neither of us wanted the version of winning that was actually on offer." Kanja picked the level back up, already sketching where the joint repair would start. "Some fights end because someone loses. That one ended because we both recognized something worth more than winning it. Took the rest of the war to find out I was right to trust that."

# What Maret Vos Chose Again

*Locked canon, Batch 264, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1369`). Captain Alias Chronicle LXIX, wave 23, closing the wave. Years after nearly walking, Maret Vos is offered an honorable way out and declines it.*

---

The offer came from Corren Halst, not Kanja, and she made a point of it being that way: Maret Vos had given the crew years now, ever since the night he'd almost walked and stayed instead on nothing but the promise that leaving would always be his to choose without owing anyone an explanation (`MCD-593`). He'd since become one of the Second Chance's steadiest hands, the kind of quietly reliable presence nobody thought to worry about anymore, which was exactly why Halst thought the offer was overdue.

"You've more than earned a clean exit if you want one," she told him, in front of no one, the way the original almost-leaving had been handled in front of no one either. "A trade, a settlement, land if you want it — whatever would actually let you build something that isn't this. Nobody would think less of you. I'd be the first one saying you'd earned it."

He thought about it for three full days, which surprised her more than an immediate answer either way would have. When he came back, it wasn't with gratitude or with the old defensiveness that had nearly driven him off the crew the first time — just a plain, considered answer.

"I know what leaving with dignity looks like now. I didn't, the first time — I thought staying or going was about pride, about not looking like I needed anyone. I know better now. And knowing that, I'm choosing to stay. Not because I still don't know how to leave. Because I've actually thought about it properly this time, and this is still what I want."

Halst didn't push further. She logged it, the way Efa Gol would have, one line in the crew's own private accounting: not a debt owed, not an obligation honored, just a free choice made twice by the same man for two entirely different reasons.

"That's the whole point of the charter," she told Kanja that night. "The first time he stayed because leaving felt like failing. This time he stayed because he actually looked at leaving and picked us anyway. Those aren't the same thing, and I wanted him to know the difference before either of us let it go unspoken any longer."

---

*Continuity notes (not narrative): a direct, deliberate callback to "The Night Maret Vos Almost Walked" (`MCD-593`), the precedent underpinning the charter's own free-membership clause (`MCD-1056`), showing the same character making the same choice years later for a genuinely different, more self-aware reason -- extending rather than repeating the original beat. Maret Vos remains he/him throughout, consistent with the Batch 226 pronoun-reconciliation ruling. No new named characters -- Maret Vos, Corren Halst, and Kanja all reused. Closes wave 23.*

# The Frost That Cracked What Fire Never Could

*Locked canon, Batch 279, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-1451`); corrected Batch 320, 2026-10-01 (Corren Halst
reconciled to he/him, matching `CC-158`). Blue-Collar Titan Alias Chronicle XCIV, wave 32, opening the wave. The alias's first winter/frost-heave hazard, distinct from every prior heat-, water-, and vapor-based crisis register.*

---

The cracking started as a sound Corren Halst almost mistook for gunfire -- a sharp, percussive snap somewhere in the rock overhead, followed by a second, then a third, spaced out like something counting.

"That's not a strike," he said, already moving crews back from the gallery ceiling. "That's timber."

Kanja pressed his palm to the nearest shoring post and felt it -- not the slow give of rot or the sudden lurch of overload, but a rhythm, tight and mean, wood fibers seizing as the hard frost above ground worked its way down through fissures that had stayed dry all autumn. Water in the stone had frozen, expanded, and was now thawing in the brief warmth of midday only to freeze again by nightfall, and every cycle was driving a wedge a little deeper into wood that had held through combat, through flooding, through fire, and had never once been built to survive being frozen and thawed forty times in a season.

"Fire we can fight," he said. "Water we can move. This is neither. This is the ground itself changing its mind twice a day."

He worked the length of the gallery with both hands flat against post after post, and it took him longer than any hazard he'd read before to understand what he was actually feeling -- not a single failure point but a whole network of small, patient stresses building in timber that looked, to the eye, exactly as sound as it had a month before. Mafesto's kinetic transfer had never been asked to track something this slow. He had to still his own breathing and hold his palms in place through three full freeze-thaw cycles, mapping which posts groaned and which held silent, before he could tell Corren Halst with any confidence which twelve needed replacing before the week was out and which forty could wait.

"You're reading the whole winter," he said, watching him work. "Not the crack. The season."

"The crack's just where the season finally said something out loud." He marked the twelve posts with chalk, then walked the rest of the gallery a second time, checking his own read against itself before he trusted it enough to pull crews off other work to act on it. "Fire tells you it's coming. Frost doesn't say anything until it's already said everything."

They replaced the twelve posts over two bitter nights, packing the new joints with a mortar mix Kanja adjusted twice to account for the coming freeze rather than the one already past, and by the time the following week's cold snap hit, the gallery held without a sound.

Corren Halst found him afterward, breath fogging in the tunnel mouth, looking back at the work with the particular satisfaction of a problem that had never needed a fight at all.

"You didn't swing anything the whole week," he said.

"Some of the worst things down here never give you anything to swing at." Kanja flexed fingers still stiff from three nights of held-still listening. "This one just wanted someone patient enough to notice it happening slow instead of waiting for it to happen fast."

---

Extends Mafesto's Kinetic Transfer System (`ARS-010`) into a new sustained, slow-timescale reading register, distinct from the density-sensing (`MCD-1068`), thermal-gradient (`MCD-1181`), and vibration-signature (`MCD-1400`) applications already locked -- this one requires holding a read across multiple freeze-thaw cycles rather than an instantaneous scan. No Trinity combat; no enemy involved. Reuses already-locked crew member Corren Halst (he/him per the Batch 320 reconciliation). No new named characters. Opens wave 32.*

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Batch 320: reconciliation corrections surfaced by the pilot fable-review pass on the Bane
Alias Chronicle corpus. Mechanical fixes (anachronisms, broken cross-references, misattributed
place names, a category-tag error) plus two pragmatic judgment calls: the Corren Halst/Danne Sok
pronoun split resolved he/him (matching majority usage, the same resolution pattern as Maret
Vos/Dol Maren, Batch 226), and the Kessic Overwatch naming collision resolved by renaming the
second, contradictory installation. No new creative facts -- pure reconciliation against
already-locked canon, matching the Batch 226/68 precedent."""
import json
from datetime import date

LEDGER_PATH = "canon-ledger.json"

SOURCE = "Pilot fable-review pass (Bane Alias Chronicle corpus), reconciliation pass, 2026-10-01"

with open(LEDGER_PATH) as f:
    ledger = json.load(f)

rules_by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in ledger["rules"]}

# --- E1: fix MCD-365's category tag ---
rules_by_id["MCD-365"]["category"] = "kanja-alias-chronicle"

# --- Amend rule statements to match the corrected Chronicle prose ---
AMENDMENTS = {
    "MCD-1391": (
        '"The White That Took the Map Away" (full narrative text at '
        "docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-white-that-took-the-map-away.md), Bane Alias Chronicle "
        "XCI, wave 31. New environmental register -- a whiteout blizzard strips Mafesto's own helm "
        "overlay of its visual advantage, forcing a detailed full-Trinity ambush defense to run "
        "entirely on sound, vibration, and Cadence Ruin. Corrected Batch 320, 2026-10-01: the "
        'original draft used an anachronistic "Sovereign Eyes" reference (that gear is built at age '
        "33, after the Trinity's own age-30 surrender, `ARS-350`, and cannot appear in a scene with "
        "Mafesto, Onyx, and Obsidian Malice all live)."
    ),
    "MCD-1425": (
        '"The Duel That Would Cost Nothing But Him" (full narrative text at '
        "docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-duel-that-would-cost-nothing-but-him.md), Bane Alias "
        "Chronicle XCV, wave 32. First entry to stage an entire engagement with the Trinity excluded "
        "from the terms before it begins rather than merely unused or malfunctioning: a garrison "
        "commander offers formal single combat, plain blade only, to decide an entire siege's "
        "outcome and spare both sides further casualties. Bane accepts on those exact terms -- Onyx "
        "sheathed, Mafesto and Obsidian Malice left with the column -- and wins through patience and "
        "Valen Sinisterblade's own in-Rebellion training as Master-at-Arms (`ARS-344`) rather than "
        "any augmented power, isolating his raw swordsmanship as the sole deciding factor for the "
        "first time since 'The Fight He Couldn't Walk Away From' (MCD-476), which still involved "
        "Onyx. The garrison surrenders whole per the wager's terms. No new named characters -- the "
        "commander is unnamed and one-scene; Corren Halst reused. Corrected Batch 320, 2026-10-01: "
        "the original draft claimed pre-Rebellion training, conflicting with `MCD-311`'s lock that "
        "Kanja's early Rebellion results came from no formal training at all, and cited the wrong "
        "rules (`MCD-291`/`292`, unrelated)."
    ),
    "MCD-1426": (
        '"What the Enemy\'s Own Children Were Owed" (full narrative text at '
        "docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/what-the-enemys-own-children-were-owed.md), Bane Alias "
        "Chronicle XCVI, wave 32, closing wave 32. First entry to extend 'the fear only works if "
        "it's true' (MCD-431) to the dependents of enemy soldiers rather than to enemies, civilians, "
        "or captives themselves: the same supply-chain sabotage that starved the Kessic Wardline "
        "garrison into surrender (MCD-700) is found to be reaching a garrison town's own military "
        "families, and Bane redirects captured grain to the civilian quarter over Corren Halst's "
        "strategic objection, stating the campaign's target was the garrison's capacity to fight, "
        "not its children's next meal. No new named characters -- the woman and her family are "
        "unnamed; Corren Halst and Danne Sok reused. Closes wave 32. Corrected Batch 320, 2026-10-01: "
        'the original draft misattributed the method to "the Threshbend depot," which fell to nine '
        "days of psychological pressure (`MCD-529`), not starvation."
    ),
    "MCD-432": (
        '"The Full Weight of the Trinity" (full narrative text at '
        "docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-full-weight-of-the-trinity.md), Bane Alias Chronicle "
        "VIII. A detailed single-combat Trinity showcase against the fortified Kessic Overwatch "
        "garrison: Mafesto's Kinetic Transfer System absorbing a six-impact volley into stored "
        "charge, Obsidian Malice discharging at full charge to breach the inner gate in one strike, "
        "and Onyx of Oblivion's Cadence Ruin/Veil Piercer breaking a trained formation into six "
        "isolated fighters, ending with the garrison's surrender and the Trinity's remaining charge "
        "deliberately left unspent. No new named characters. Corrected Batch 320, 2026-10-01: the "
        'original draft specified a "two years of dormant charge" figure for Obsidian Malice that '
        "duplicates the bank already spent at the Black Trench weeks earlier (`ARS-342`); reworded "
        "to a plain full discharge."
    ),
    "MCD-1060": (
        '"The Twelve Miles That Never Stopped Moving" (full narrative text at '
        "docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/the-twelve-miles-that-never-stopped-moving.md), Bane Alias "
        "Chronicle LXII, wave 21. Rebellion era, within the \"Bane\" window -- not a territory "
        "Chronicle. A detailed full-Trinity combat showcase built around continuous motion rather "
        "than a held position: a six-hundred-refugee convoy, a wounded rearguard, and a pursuing "
        "Directorate cavalry screen force a twelve-mile defense across three changing terrains "
        "without the column's pace ever dropping below a walk. Across open grassland, Mafesto's "
        "Kinetic Transfer System redirects charging cavalry's own momentum sideways through Bane's "
        "footing mid-stride. Through a close pine stand, Onyx of Oblivion's Cadence Ruin folds an "
        "infantry bottleneck attempt apart while Veil Piercer picks two disguised scouts out of a "
        "civilian-looking knot mid-stride. Along a final exposed causeway, Obsidian Malice is "
        "released at full discharge in one arcing blast timed to the pursuing commander's committed "
        "final push, delivered without Bane breaking stride to aim it. The column crosses the "
        "border zone an hour before dusk having never once formed up to fight from fixed ground. "
        "Distinguished from every prior full-Trinity showcase (the fortified-garrison assault, "
        "MCD-432; the multi-day siege, MCD-529; the vertical battlement fight, MCD-703; the "
        "precision-constrained bridge defense, MCD-1026; and the most-intense ravine battle, "
        "MCD-709) by its continuous-motion constraint. No new named characters -- Efa Gol reused; "
        "the pursuing Directorate commander is unnamed and one-scene. Second entry in wave 21. "
        "Corrected Batch 320, 2026-10-01: the original draft specified a duplicate 'two years of "
        "dormant charge' figure for Obsidian Malice; reworded to a plain full discharge."
    ),
}

for rid, new_statement in AMENDMENTS.items():
    rules_by_id[rid]["statement"] = new_statement

# --- C5: new CC- dossiers for Corren Halst and Danne Sok (he/him pronoun reconciliation) ---
NEW_RULES = [
    {
        "id": "CC-158",
        "category": "character-dossier",
        "statement": (
            "Corren Halst: he/him (reconciled Batch 320, 2026-10-01, resolving a real pronoun "
            "split -- he/him throughout the Bane Alias Chronicle corpus, but she/her in a number of "
            "Captain and Blue-Collar Titan entries -- in favor of the clear majority usage, the same "
            "resolution pattern as Maret Vos/Dol Maren, Batch 226). One of the three earliest crew "
            "members freed independently before Maw-9, by the Black Trench (age 19, `MCD-234`), "
            "alongside Danne Sok and Maret Vos, forming the nucleus of Kanja's earliest crew before "
            "the mass liberation. Serves as Bane's second and most heavily recurring confidant across "
            "the Bane Alias Chronicle corpus (34+ waves), later taking a rotating dispute-council "
            "chair term under the Captain-era charter (`MCD-1056`/`1380`) and, decades on, a "
            "dock-era leg injury forces a graceful transition from front-line rotation to training "
            "the crew's recruits (`MCD-1459`)."
        ),
        "status": "locked",
        "source": SOURCE,
    },
    {
        "id": "CC-159",
        "category": "character-dossier",
        "statement": (
            "Danne Sok: he/him (reconciled Batch 320, 2026-10-01, same resolution as `CC-158`). One "
            "of the three earliest crew members freed independently before Maw-9, by the Black "
            "Trench (age 19, `MCD-234`), alongside Corren Halst and Maret Vos. Runs an "
            "intelligence/verification network referenced extensively across the Bane Alias "
            "Chronicle corpus (e.g. independently confirming a Directorate defector's account over "
            "six weeks, `MCD-1027`). Privately kept, for the whole of the war, a memory of the young "
            "Kanja's hands shaking for an hour after freeing him, before any alias existed (`MCD-530`). "
            "Has a daughter (deliberately kept unnamed) who grows up visiting the crew's ships and "
            "eventually enlists, leading her own first independent operation a generation after "
            "Corren Halst's own comparable growth (`MCD-1002`/`1517`)."
        ),
        "status": "locked",
        "source": SOURCE,
    },
]

existing_ids = set(rules_by_id.keys())
for r in NEW_RULES:
    assert r["id"] not in existing_ids, f"ID collision: {r['id']}"
    ledger["rules"].append(r)

ledger["batches_completed"].append({
    "batch": 320,
    "date": str(date.today()),
    "source": SOURCE,
    "rule_count": len(NEW_RULES),
    "note": (
        "Reconciliation pass following the pilot fable-review of the Bane Alias Chronicle corpus "
        "(the pilot chunk for a much larger proposed corpus-wide review, which the pilot's own "
        "measured cost -- ~150-170K tokens for one 108-file chunk -- showed would be prohibitively "
        "expensive to run in full without first fixing the chunking methodology). Fixed: a "
        "Trinity-era anachronism (Sovereign Eyes appearing before it's built, MCD-1391), an "
        "Iron-Bastard-doctrine anachronism (MCD-709), Obsidian Malice's 'two years of dormant "
        "charge' claimed redundantly within 18 months of the Black Trench across three entries "
        "(MCD-432, MCD-709, MCD-1060), a mislabeled pre-Rebellion Valen-training claim and wrong "
        "citation (MCD-1425), a misattributed broken-promise settlement name (MCD-939), a "
        "misattributed siege method plus a leaked inline rule-ID citation (MCD-1426), a grief "
        "reference pointed at a battle already locked as zero-casualty (MCD-693), a Dol Maren trait "
        "bled onto Maret Vos (MCD-1061), a mis-tagged category on Bane's actual Chronicle I "
        "(MCD-365), two Voice-Bible characterization labels leaking into narrative prose as quoted "
        "in-world phrases (MCD-706, MCD-1027), a writers'-room 'wave' reference leaking into prose "
        "(MCD-1393), Obsidian Malice described as a bladed/sheathed weapon twice (MCD-1100, "
        "MCD-1113), a misattributed waystation-song callback (MCD-1432), stale Chronicle-count "
        "figures and a stale citation in the Bane profile doc and tracker. Two pragmatic judgment "
        "calls made directly per Abad's 'proceeding a pragmatic order' direction rather than "
        "blocking on separate rulings: (1) Corren Halst and Danne Sok's real pronoun split "
        "(confirmed by corpus-wide grep: he/him in all of Bane, but she/her in 7 Captain/"
        "Blue-Collar Titan entries) resolved he/him for both, the clear majority usage, with new "
        "dossiers locked at CC-158/159 and every affected file swept; (2) the Kessic Overwatch "
        "naming collision (one entry has it taken by a violent full-Trinity assault, MCD-432; "
        "another has the same name surrender cleanly on amnesty terms six weeks earlier, MCD-1102) "
        "resolved by renaming the second, contradictory installation to a distinct garrison, "
        "Hallmere, rather than forcing either account to fit the other -- the same resolution "
        "pattern already used elsewhere in the project for this exact class of collision. Pure "
        "reconciliation throughout -- no new creative facts beyond the two dossiers, matching the "
        "Batch 226/68 precedent."
    ),
})

ledger["ledger_version"] = round(ledger["ledger_version"] + 0.1, 1)
ledger["last_updated"] = str(date.today())

ids = [r["id"] for r in ledger["rules"]]
assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "Duplicate rule IDs detected!"

with open(LEDGER_PATH, "w") as f:
    json.dump(ledger, f, indent=2)
    f.write("\n")

print(f"OK: {len(ledger['rules'])} total rules, {len(ledger['batches_completed'])} batches, "
      f"ledger_version {ledger['ledger_version']}, zero duplicate IDs.")

Do NOT commit.

## Fixes to apply

**C1 — Sephtis's death (RULING: reframe as staged/theatrical, not a real death).** Sephtis (Vrail, CC-037, 1,997 years old) is locked as alive in present-day/Book-4 era elsewhere in canon (he can't actually die of old age in this track). Edit `MCD-982`'s file (find it via the rule statement -> file path) so the "death" is explicitly a staged withdrawal/retirement cover: he fakes a natural death and sea-burial that the lineage genuinely believes, while actually continuing on elsewhere during the Long Mask in disguise (consistent with a 2,000-year-old operative choosing to let a mortal identity "die" rather than explain his own longevity). Add a sentence making this explicit in MCD-982's own file and continuity note. Then update the downstream files/statements that assert he is "deceased"/"dead" as fact: MCD-983, MCD-1348, MCD-1357, MCD-1513 (reword "his own death" / "generations after his own death" / "decades gone" type lines to "after he stepped back and let the world believe he'd died" or similar — keep the lineage's own belief and grief genuine, just make clear to the reader it was staged, not real).

**C2 — Full Trinity combat in entries set decades past the age-30 surrender (`MCD-246`).** Affected files (find via rule IDs): MCD-588, 589, 907, 984, 1053, 1087, 1338, 1341, 1350, 1353, 1419, 1506, 1510, 1511, 1512. Apply the standard swap: Mafesto's Kinetic Transfer System -> Forge-Coat + Ironfall Boots grounding function; Obsidian Malice discharge -> Ironhand Gauntlets leverage/plain striking (never call it a "discharge"); Onyx of Oblivion's named powers / "reading" a fight -> the Rexmar Machete + Kanja's own instinctive Rexmar-Mar tactical sense, with Sovereign Eyes/Smoke System covering perception/stealth beats. Keep every scene/beat/outcome identical — only the gear/mechanism performing each action changes. MCD-1419's line "three generations of Trinity use had taught him" needs rewording (no Trinity by this point). MCD-1506's "equipment failure" beat should transfer to Smoke System capsules or Ironhand plates. MCD-1512's "without Onyx at his hip" becomes "without the Rexmar Machete at his hip" or similar. Update each file's header note citing this correction batch, and update the corresponding rule statements (for your merge script).

**C3 — Fourth-generation apprentice's sex flips mid-track.** Majority usage is he/him (10 entries: MCD-1343,1344,1345,1349,1354,1357,1358,1359,1360,1362) vs she/her (5 entries: MCD-1419,1420,1505,1509,1512). RULING: go with the majority, he/him. Fix the 5 minority files (MCD-1419, 1420, 1505, 1509, 1512) and their rule statements to he/him.

**C4 — Internal timeline slips.** MCD-1088 "a season ago" should be "three years ago" (to match MCD-1086/1337's "three years"). MCD-1349's "fifteen-year peace" should be reworded to fit roughly a five-year span (match MCD-1354's "two years earlier" relative framing) — reword to "a handful of years' peace" or similar.

## Mechanical errors (apply all)

- **E1 duplicate numerals:** wave 5 (MCD-555/556/557) is wrongly numbered XVI/XVII/XVIII; renumber to XIII/XIV/XV in both file headers and rule statements (wave 6, MCD-561/562/563, correctly keeps XVI-XVIII).
- **E2 writers'-room leaks in prose:** MCD-505 ("the fourth wave"), MCD-1350 ("two waves earlier"), MCD-1352 ("two waves back"), MCD-1359 ("two waves earlier," "two entries earlier"), MCD-1363 ("thirty waves now"), MCD-1418 ("seven waves back"), MCD-1420 ("Thirty waves"), MCD-1505 ("wave after wave ago"). Replace with in-world time phrasing ("two seasons back," "years ago," etc.).
- **E3 rule-ID citations leaked into prose:** MCD-1349, 1357, 1505, 1507, 1508, 1510, 1512 all have literal `MCD-xxxx` citations inside narrative sentences. Remove the parenthetical citations from the prose (keep them only in the continuity notes section).
- **E4 Obsidian Malice mischaracterized as a blade / attributed to Onyx:** MCD-907 ("the blade's raw kinetic output"), MCD-1341, MCD-1353 (both call it "Onyx's Obsidian Malice"). Fix: Obsidian Malice is a war club (ARS-030) and is Mafesto/Kanja's own weapon, not one of Onyx's named powers. Reword accordingly.
- **E5 wrong citation:** MCD-1352 cites MCD-241 for Ghost Harbor's renaming; correct citation is MCD-235.
- **E6 tech anachronism:** MCD-1087 "engine-heat signature" — this world has no engines beyond the Hymn-Engine/Meridian Engine. Reword to "lantern-heat signature" or "galley-fire signature."
- **E7 real-world calendar name:** MCD-1361 "most of the ordinary Tuesdays in between" -> "most of the ordinary days in between."
- **E9 stale tracker:** in `docs/lords-of-cian/chronicle-tracks-status.md`, find the Storm That Walks row and change its Chronicle count from 93 to 102.

input.prompt:

**C2 — Halst/Sok/Vos origin story, three incompatible versions (RULING: adopt the manuscript's own locked account as highest authority).** The already-locked manuscript (Chronicle III, Batch 70) says: "three fighters who had found each other on the docks before they found Kanja — three survivors of the Maws," freed independently. MCD-533 (Vos) and MCD-641 (Sok) wrongly say Kanja personally freed them — fix both to say they were Maw survivors who found each other on the docks, then found Kanja (not freed by his hand). MCD-1137 (Halst) has her freed from a "work-camp" by a different rebellion cell — change "work-camp" to "one of the Maws" and reframe the three-weeks-observation beat as happening after she'd already found Halst/Sok on the docks, or after reaching the docks herself. Draft a new ledger rule `CC-160`: a dossier for Maret Vos (he/him, per CC-158/159's own precedent) establishing this same Maw-survivor/docks origin, written in the same style as CC-158 (Corren Halst) and CC-159 (Danne Sok) — read those two rules in canon-ledger.json for the exact tone/format to match. Also draft an amendment to CC-158 and CC-159 adding one clause each: "found each other on the docks before finding Kanja, all three Maw survivors" (keep everything else in those two rules unchanged).

**C3 — Garren Hask's recruitment (MCD-623) misattributed.** CC-115 and the manuscript lock Hask's recruitment as happening when Forge-7 evidence confirmed his wife's suspicions (pre-alias, pre-Dredge-Line), age 53. MCD-623 wrongly frames it as a post-Dredge-Line recruitment via overhearing a tally at Silt Row. Rewrite MCD-623's file so it's not a recruitment scene at all — reframe it as the moment Hask formally took over the ledger-keeping role within the crew (a promotion/responsibility moment, not his first meeting with Kanja), set it chronologically before the Dredge-Line Ambush, and fix any "31-year-old" age reference to 53 (31 was CC-115's tenure-in-years, misread as his age).

**C4 — Dredge-Line kill count vs. "no killing" doctrine.** MCD-1129 says "The canal that had drowned two hundred soldiers the year before" — this contradicts the Dredge-Line Ambush's established doctrine (drowns the enemy's density advantage/equipment, not a literal 200-person body count) and the locked Kanja profile's "no killing" doctrine. Reword MCD-1129's line to remove the specific "two hundred soldiers" death toll — something like "The canal that had broken the column's advantage the year before" or similar, preserving the scene's tone without the kill-count claim.

**C5 — Tavin Greer's allegiance (MCD-644).** Greer is locked as an active Directorate officer who never claims credit (MCD-1131, MCD-403). MCD-644 has him teaching a crew-apparatus clerk as if he's inside the rebellion's own structure. Fix: change "assigned to the five-district cross-checking work" (crew-internal) to describe a Trust/Directorate clerk instead, so Greer stays consistently on the Directorate side throughout.

**C6 — Dol Maren's plank-bridges.** CC-121 locks the seventeen plank-bridges as built/load-tested AT the Dredge-Line Ambush itself. MCD-1123 wrongly has them built "in the weeks after the flood." Fix MCD-1123's wording to say they were built during/for the ambush itself, not afterward.

## Mechanical errors (apply all)

- **E1:** MCD-627 introduces "Ondrej Vask" — "Vask" collides with Lauris's locked Karesian institutional term (Vask Karth-Ven etc., 52 ledger hits). Rename to a different surname (collision-check your choice against canon-ledger.json first). MCD-637 introduces "Ruven Calx" in prose while its rule statement says "no new named characters" — just fix the rule statement to note Ruven Calx as a new, collision-checked-clean minor character.
- **E2 wrong citations:** MCD-1029's note wrongly cites MCD-449 (should be MCD-624); MCD-1127's note wrongly cites MCD-291 (should be ARS-010/MCD-232); MCD-1436's header wrongly lists "MCD-403-adjacent" (should be MCD-632).
- **E3:** MCD-650 has Pell Ostra referred to in third person incorrectly and cites "accelerant work at Coldrace" when MCD-648's Coldrace job was incident-free — fix the self-reference and remove/adjust the accelerant claim.
- **E4:** MCD-944 title/header says "two weeks"/"fortnight" but body says "three weeks" — make consistent (pick three weeks, matching the body).
- **E5:** MCD-1147 garbled sentence "four years older than the boy who had chalked three words" should read "four years older than Kanja" (Callum Breck, per CC-117).
- **E6:** MCD-900 "three years of Onyx-work" is impossible (Onyx only bonds at age 17, per ARS-020, and this is pre-Black-Trench so at most ~2 years) — change "three years" to "a year or more" or similar.
- **E7:** MCD-629 header says "years before" the Black Trench when it's actually less than a year away, and the ravine was sealed not opened by the charges (MCD-232) — fix "years before" to "months before" and "would open" to "would seal." Also it garbles CC-133 (Pell Ostra scaled the Scrip-Forge accelerant to detonate the Dead Drakma stockpile, not "the Scrip-Forge stockpile at Ash-Wharf") — fix the wording to match CC-133.
- **E8:** MCD-1435 says "one of the first fourteen names" but MCD-1031 establishes sixteen students (fourteen was just the request count) — fix MCD-1435 to clarify it was one of the fourteen originally requested, out of sixteen total trained.
- **E9 writers'-room/label leaks:** MCD-480 ("the clean, decisive powers showcase the line had heard about") and MCD-1129 (quotes a Chronicle title "the 'Line That Wouldn't Break' kind of defense" in-world) — reword both to plain in-world phrasing. MCD-1127 references "Angle-Whisper" (Varruk's Triad-Guardian ability, CC-051/098) with no in-scene grounding for age-18 Kanja — remove that specific comparison, describe the sensation plainly instead.
- **E10:** MCD-1062's note falsely claims "Kessic flats is new geography" when Kessic already exists elsewhere in the ledger (Bane's Kessic Overwatch/Wardline). Rename "Kessic flats" to a different, collision-checked-clean name, OR note explicitly it's the same broader Kessic region (pick whichever reads better in context — your call, just make it consistent).
- **E11:** Onyx's "Whisper of Shadows" power is used inconsistently as a structural/door-opening effect in MCD-1439 ("against the door hinge itself," taking a door off its frame) — that function belongs to Veil Piercer (MCD-636/1433), not Whisper of Shadows. Fix MCD-1439 to attribute the door effect to Veil Piercer instead.
- **E13:** MCD-1441 calls Nev Torr "a frightened conscript's boy" — Torr is established as a riveter's apprentice/dockhand Callum Breck brought in, not a conscript. Fix the description.

Delete that clause from the note and statement; describe it as a plain chimney-signal code with no gear citation.

- **E7:** MCD-1004 has Kanja say "I built the Trinity to survive a rebellion" (he recovered/bonded Onyx, didn't build the Trinity, per ARS-020) and references "whatever comes after" being unclear about "it," when the actual question Hask asked was about the ship/crew. Fix the dialogue to remove "I built the Trinity" framing — reword to reflect Kanja recovering/bonding rather than building, and clarify "this crew" is what the uncertainty is about, not "the Trinity."
- **E8:** MCD-1518 internally contradicts itself — "He came without the Forge-Coat sealed for impact" vs. later "the Forge-Coat's plating and the Ironfall Boots' grounding soles took the collective shove." Fix so he's consistently wearing or not wearing the coat throughout (your call — pick whichever fits the scene's point better).
- **E9:** MCD-429 has Obsidian Malice's "recharge cycle" given a 40-second framing when ARS-030 locks a 3-5 second recharge — fix to remove the specific "40 seconds... wouldn't have cleared in time" framing, reword to "there wasn't room for a second swing." MCD-558 wrongly attributes reduced sleep need to Mafesto's KTS (a force-redirect system, not a biology system) — fix to attribute it to Kanja's own biology (the entry already says this two lines later — just remove the Mafesto misattribution). MCD-596 says "the Trinity's resting density" — resting density belongs to Kanja (MCD-293), not "the Trinity" — fix the attribution.
- **E10:** MCD-1374/1521 describe the Sovereign Eyes' amber glow as a night-vision/perception function ("predator-glow low-light function," "the glow picking out heat and motion") — per ARS-350 the glow is what OTHERS see (a fear-response signal); the actual perception comes from the Blueprint-Eye HUD overlay. Fix both to say "the Sovereign Eyes' overlay" instead of "glow" for the perception function.
- **E11 stale tracker/profile:** in `docs/lords-of-cian/chronicle-tracks-status.md`, Captain row says 93; change to 102. In `docs/lords-of-cian/character-profiles/alias-captain.md`: fix the claim that the nine Batch-314 entries are "full-Trinity combat showcases" (they're not, post-fix); fix the claim that Long Mask gear "appears nowhere in the Captain track" (it does, extensively); fix the claim that Halst/Sok/Vos "have no dedicated CC- dossier" (CC-158/159 now exist); fix "her term's actual end" for Halst to "his"; fix the false claim of an XCII duplicate (there isn't one — the second hit is a different alias's entry, MCD-1486, cross-referencing this track).
- **E12:** Minor — MCD-606 says "the first year after the Black Trench" (age 20) while Breck speaks of "years after his own recovered voice" (he recovered at age 21) — adjust for consistency if easy, otherwise skip.

When done, report: the full list of edited files, the merge script path, and a one-paragraph summary.

input.prompt:
Repo: /home/user/Lords-of-Cian-Knowledge-Core ("My Rival's Distance: The Lords of Cian" canon project). A read-only review of "The Scourge" Alias Chronicle track (102 entries, the 284-year Long Mask disguise identity, ages 22-314) already ran and found specific contradictions/errors. Your job: apply the fixes directly to the Chronicle files (edit prose + header notes), and separately prepare (but do NOT run) a Python merge script that would amend the affected canon-ledger.json rule statements. Do NOT touch canon-ledger.json or git yourself — write the merge script to `merge_batch321_scourge_fixes.py` in the repo root (read an existing `merge_batch320_*.py` in the repo root first for the exact JSON pattern) and report back its path plus the full file list you edited. Do NOT commit.

## Fixes to apply

**C1 — Mafesto and Obsidian Malice (Trinity gear, surrendered at age 30 per MCD-246) used throughout the Long Mask across 17 entries (the Onyx-sealed check came back clean — this is specifically about Mafesto/Obsidian Malice).** Apply the standard swap-map to all of these: MCD-446, 492, 543, 802, 805, 808, 812, 817, 823, 829, 1041, 1074, 1075, 1469, 1470, 1471, 1476. Swap: Mafesto's Kinetic Transfer System -> the Forge-Coat + Ironfall Boots grounding weave; Obsidian Malice's discharge -> the Ironhand Gauntlets' leverage (never call it a "discharge"); any "Trinity" references implying possession ("no amount of Trinity gear," "no Trinity relic that mattered," "the Trinity and the loadout together") -> reword to reference the Long Mask gear system (ARS-344-356) instead. Also remove every "two-year dormant charge/cycle" claim in these same files (MCD-446, 802, 805, 829) — Obsidian Malice doesn't exist as active gear in this era at all post-swap, so those lines should simply be removed/reworded as part of the swap. Leave MCD-1014 and MCD-1015 (ages 24/27) UNCHANGED — they are correctly pre-seal, legitimate Trinity use. Update the 8 rule statements that explicitly assert Mafesto/Obsidian Malice (MCD-446, 492, 543, 802, 1041, 1074, 1469, 1471) plus the 3 soft "Trinity" statements (MCD-1232, 1242, 1476) to match the Long Mask gear framing.

**C2 — Kanja's locked late-Long-Mask physical decline (ages 205+) contradicts this track's hands-on physical feats at the same ages (RULING: option (a) — read the decline as genuinely intermittent, "good days vs bad days," and soften the two entries that most need it rather than touching the already-locked MCD-1022 ending).** Fix MCD-1406 (age 313, personally moving 81 people down a beach in 40 minutes) and the boarding-action beats in MCD-1022 (age 314, pike-deflection/hatch-slamming) so the successor and crew do more of the hands-on physical work while Kanja directs/assists at a reduced capacity consistent with "on bad days... on good days" (MCD-271). Do NOT rewrite MCD-1022's actual ending or outcome — just soften which character performs which specific physical actions. Leave MCD-1235(238)/1249(260)/1239(262)/1074(268)/1232(250) as-is for now (do not re-age them) — this is a judgment call beyond mechanical fixing; just make the MCD-1406/1022 adjustment.

**C3 — "V3 until 241 / V4 debut at 241" contradicts ARS-348 (Forge-Coat V4 = ages 180-284) (RULING: reframe MCD-811's "new coat" as a Sovereign Eyes V4 refit rather than a new Forge-Coat version).** Fix MCD-811 ("The First Night in the New Coat," age 241): reframe the six-years-in-development item as the Sovereign Eyes V4 refit (ARS-350 locks V4 starting at age 240+, which fits) rather than a new Forge-Coat version — keep the lens-glare teething beat, since that fits Sovereign Eyes perfectly. Then fix the ~20 rule statements/continuity notes citing "ARS-348, ages 80-241" or "V4 debut age 241 per MCD-811" (MCD-1076, 1229-1250, 1406-1408, 1469-1477) to cite the correct ARS-348 ranges instead (V3 = ages 80-180, V4 = 180-284) and the Sovereign Eyes V4 reframing where relevant. Fix the dozen entries tagged "V3 gear" between ages 180-240 (MCD-830, 1043, 1233, 1248, 1250, 1469, 1244, 1237, 1474, 1076, 1235, 1475) to correctly say "V4 gear" instead (since V4 starts at 180 per ARS-348, not 241).

**C4 — The Salt Keep's own date is inconsistent (RULING: lock age 140, matching MCD-446/545/1476's own rule text; fix the earlier references to point at a different liberation).** Fix MCD-801 (age 36, "We know what you did to the Salt Keep") and MCD-819 (age 55, "cleared the Salt Keep two years ago") — swap both references to a different, earlier, era-appropriate liberation instead (e.g. a Pirate Dawn-era galleon liberation, MCD-381) since the Salt Keep hasn't happened yet at those ages. Fix MCD-491 (age ~110, "the same clean liberation he'd delivered at the Salt Keep") similarly. Fix MCD-807 (age 150, "the morning after the Salt Keep's harbor siege" — ten years too late, and MCD-446 was a wall-breach not a harbor siege) to "years after the Salt Keep" or similar, removing the false "morning after" immediacy and the "harbor siege" mischaracterization. Fix MCD-809 (age 165, "founded by Salt Keep survivors two decades past" — puts the Keep at ~145, five years off) to "roughly twenty-five years past" (puts it at 140). Fix MCD-1476 (age 175, "no one had raided anything here in eleven years" implies age 164) to "no one had raided anything here in thirty-five years" (fits age 140).

**C5 — MCD-1229 (age 98) wrongly re-enters Garren Hask's sealed testimony from MCD-1018 (age 148, which hasn't happened yet).** Fix MCD-1229's statement and continuity note to drop the MCD-1018 linkage — the prose already hedges with "a different court, over the Scrip-Forge evidence," so just remove the explicit MCD-1018 citation from the statement/note. Then check MCD-1250 (age 200, "a hundred and two years" referencing MCD-1229's age) — if it depends on MCD-1229 being ~98, it should still work fine (200-98=102) since you're not changing MCD-1229's own age, just its false MCD-1018 linkage — no further change needed there.

**C6 — "Efa Gol's successor" acting before the age-150 handoff (locked in MCD-807).** Fix MCD-820 (age 133) and MCD-822 (age 145) — both have "Efa Gol's successor" running reputation analysis/briefing Kanja before the handoff. Change "Efa Gol's successor" to "Efa Gol" herself in both files (she hasn't retired yet at these ages).

**C7 — Backward references to entries that happen later.** Fix MCD-823 (age 160): "the way Sovereign Eyes had once read a reef no chart recorded" references MCD-812 (age 255, hasn't happened yet) — reword to remove the specific forward reference, describe the Sovereign Eyes' capability generically instead. Fix MCD-1239 (age 262): "built originally against cold water and pack ice" references MCD-1074 (age 268, hasn't happened yet) — reword to remove the forward reference.

**C8 — Early gear-version drift (ages 36-140).** Fix MCD-381 (Pirate Dawn, ages 48-52): "the Forge-Coat V1... still crude... twelve kilograms" — V1 is ages 33-40 per ARS-347 Pirate Dawn overlaps the V1/V2 boundary; check ARS-347's exact ranges and relabel to V2 if the age fits, or adjust MCD-381's stated age downward slightly if cleaner. Also fix "Terror mode" smoke reference if Terror mode is locked as a V3-only feature per ARS-354 — remove or reword if so. Fix MCD-801's note calling age 36 "roughly a year after The Shape the Smoke Remembers" (MCD-381 is actually 12-16 years earlier) — correct the elapsed time. Fix MCD-446 (age 140): "the Forge-Coat's V2 grounding weave" should be "V3" (or V4, depending on how you resolved C3 above — check your own C3 fix and make this consistent).

**C9 — Span arithmetic conflates "since Ash-Wharf" (age 22) with "the 284-year Long Mask" (which starts at age 30).** Fix MCD-1022 (age 314): "Two hundred and eighty-four years... since a morning on a burned wharf" should be "two hundred and ninety-two years" (314-22=292) OR reword to "the Long Mask's two hundred and eighty-four years" (avoiding the Ash-Wharf-specific count). Fix MCD-1255 (age 313) similarly: "two hundred and eighty-three years" -> "two hundred and ninety-one years" or reword to avoid the Ash-Wharf anchor. Leave MCD-813 (305) and MCD-1477 (258) unchanged — they already count correctly from age 22.

**C10 — MCD-1244 (age 215) has an impossible timeline for the 211-captive galleon fight.** "decades before any of this gear existed" and "twenty years" of gauntlet technique — but MCD-381's galleon fight was itself ALREADY a gear showcase (Forge-Coat, Gauntlets, Boots), and the actual span between ages 48-52 and 215 is roughly 165 years, not "decades"/"twenty years." Fix MCD-1244 to remove the false "before any of this gear existed" claim and correct "twenty years" to "a century and more" or similar.

## Mechanical errors (apply all)

- **E1:** MCD-382 has a rule-ID leaked into prose: "MCD-250's own account of surrender-on-sight without verification" — strip the citation, reword to plain prose.
- **E2:** MCD-1015's prose has an alias misattribution: "Bane. The one from the Furnace District before that" — the Furnace District Strike belongs to the Industrial Myth alias (MCD-244), not Bane. Fix the dialogue reference. Note: this rule's STATEMENT says "Trench Monarch" — check which one is actually correct per the Furnace District Strike's real owner (Industrial Myth) and fix both the prose and statement to be consistent and correct.
- **E3:** MCD-1407 places Sena's near-kill "in a market square" while MCD-1043 sets it on a ship's deck after a boarding — fix MCD-1407 to match MCD-1043's deck setting. MCD-1408 says "more than eighty individually followed lives" where MCD-1407 gives 41 — fix MCD-1408's number to be consistent with MCD-1407 (41, or a clearly-labeled larger cumulative total if that's what's intended — your call, just make them consistent).
- **E4:** MCD-1235 self-contradicts: "triggered eleven times across the alias's life... This became the tenth." Fix to make the numbers consistent (pick one, e.g. "This became the eleventh").
- **E5 elapsed-time slips (fix each to be internally consistent with its own cross-referenced entry):** MCD-1471 "fourteen years before" should reference MCD-1017 correctly — check the actual gap and fix the number. You are doing a read-only contradiction/error/enrichment review for a long-running canon-locking project ("My Rival's Distance: The Lords of Cian" by Abad Morel), repo root /home/user/Lords-of-Cian-Knowledge-Core. ## Your scope: Phase 1.5 of a corpus-wide review roadmap — the World Atlas

This is the "Atlas" phase, which follows a just-completed Phase 1 (a full fable-review-then-fix pass across all 11 Alias Chronicle tracks, ~990 Chronicles, Batches 320-330 — see CLAUDE.md's "Phase 1" section near the end for what was found and fixed there). Several of those Phase 1 passes surfaced real place-name problems that got patched locally (renames to resolve collisions) but were never checked against the Atlas as a whole. Your job is to do that whole-Atlas consistency check now, before further geography-touching work happens.

Read these first:
1. `canon-ledger.json` — grep for all rules with id prefix `GEO-` (there are 6: GEO-001 through GEO-006) and read their full statements. These lock the Regional Atlas: 11 named regions, canon-locked Capital/Maw sites, ~52 free-to-rename Holds/Settlements, and two Jicome-region narrative sites (Killane, Ghost Harbor) added later.
2. `research/atlas-live-sheet-audit.md` if it exists — the audit that originally reconciled the ledger against the live Google Sheet Atlas.
3. The full canon-ledger.json for every other geography-touching rule you can find — grep for region/location keywords, settlement names, "Hold", "Settlement", "Maw-", "Karkosa", etc., especially anything under MCD-, ARS-, MAW-, POL- prefixes that names a place.

## What to check

Grep the entire `docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/` corpus (1,500+ files) for place names and cross-check them against the Atlas rules (GEO-001 through GEO-006) and against each other. Specifically look for:

1. **Place names invented in Chronicle prose that were never placed on the Atlas** — a settlement, Hold, landmark, or region mentioned in Chronicle text with no corresponding GEO- rule or Gazetteer entry. Flag the highest-traffic ones (mentioned across multiple Chronicles) as priority.
2. **Collisions already patched in Phase 1 that need Atlas-level reconciliation**: Kessic Overwatch vs. Hallmere (Batch 320's resolution — a renamed garrison), Kessara vs. Varrow, Ferrenline vs. Orencliff docks (Batch 329's Scourge-track renames). Confirm these renamed locations now have a consistent, collision-free place in the Atlas's own naming space, and that no other Chronicle anywhere in the corpus still uses the OLD, now-wrong name post-rename.
3. **Killane's real geography** — GEO-006 placed Killane as a Corehold-class fortress-city Hold within Jicome's grid. Cross-check every Chronicle that mentions Killane (there should be many — it's a recurring Blue-Collar Titan/Iron Bastard site) for geography consistent with that placement (region, neighboring sites, travel times/distances implied).
4. **Unplaced invented naval/territory geography** flagged during Phase 1 — search Sovereign Ghost of the Great Sea, Crow King, Lord of Embers, and Trench Monarch Chronicles specifically for invented straits, reefs, harbors, coastal settlements, or territories that appear repeatedly but were never locked onto the Atlas (e.g., "Ghost Harbor" status — is it actually in GEO-006 already? verify).
5. **Internal Atlas consistency** — do GEO-001 through GEO-006 themselves contradict each other or contain any gaps/typos now that more material exists to check against them?
6. **Real-world place name leaks** — scan for any accidental real-world geographic proper nouns that violate the project's standing no-real-world-proper-nouns convention (distinct from the deliberate real-vocabulary-reuse pattern used for territory/alias names).

## Output format

Produce a structured report:
- CONTRADICTIONS: direct conflicts between two already-locked facts (geography that can't both be true)
- ERRORS: a single wrong/inconsistent/unplaced geographic claim
- ENRICHMENT: real gaps worth filling (an unplaced but load-bearing location) grouped into clusters
- METRICS: token/agent-call cost estimate for this pass, so the orchestrating session can calibrate future phases

For each finding, give: exact file(s)/rule ID(s) affected, a precise description of the problem, and a recommended fix (not a full rewrite — just the fix instruction, since a separate Sonnet-model agent will apply your exact instructions verbatim). Do not edit any files — this is read-only review only. Be thorough but efficient; you don't need to read every single one of 1,500+ Chronicle files in full — targeted grep searches for place-name keywords across the corpus, combined with full reads of the Atlas-relevant rules, is the right approach.

Report back in full detail — your report will be read directly by the orchestrating session, which will then apply fixes.

  - **Downstream:** the Ozmund strand then treated `MCD-147`'s "already-locked Verehimu Wetlands" as House Verehimu's own holdings and planted settlements in it — Greyfen (`MCD-1738`, `MCD-1775`, `MCD-1838`, `MCD-1847`; 10 corpus files), Sennick (`MCD-1789`, `MCD-1796`), plus `ozmund-chronicle-ix/xlvi/lx/lxv`. The Crow King track (`the-second-scarecrow.md`, `the-return-to-the-wetlands.md`, `before-the-marsh.md`, `three-hundred-voices-one-lie.md`) and `lauris-chronicle-xxiv` use "Voskharen Wetlands". Nothing says whether these are one wetland or two; the Blueprint's text (where MCD-147 came from) says one.
  - **Fix (needs Abad's one-line ruling; recommended path = two distinct places, minimal edits):** (1) amend `MCD-147` in place: "the Verehimu Wetlands" → "the Voskharen Wetlands (renamed from the source's 'Verehimu' per the Batch 36/41 standing rename)". (2) add one clarifying sentence to `MCD-1738`: "The Verehimu Wetlands of this strand are House Verehimu's own wetland holdings near the House seat — a distinct location from the Voskharen Wetlands of Jicome's coast (`MCD-236`), not the `MCD-147` deposit region." No Chronicle prose changes needed under this path. Alternative (if Abad wants one wetland): rename the Ozmund strand's four files + `MCD-1738/1789/1775/1838/1847/1796` to Voskharen — larger, not recommended.
  
  ### C3. "Aboard the Karkosa" — Karkosa is both the Sovereign Trust's capital city and, in ten Blueprint-era rules, the Lords of Cian's own home base/vessel
  - **Rules:** `MCD-156`, `MCD-169`, `MCD-206`, `MCD-211` say Lauris keeps her archive "**aboard** the Karkosa"; `MCD-196` ("the Karkosa's archive room"), `MCD-199`/`MCD-203` ("the Karkosa's primary forge"), `MCD-208` ("the Karkosa's home harbor … around Kanja's operational presence"), `MCD-212` ("the Karkosa's senior crew"), `MCD-226` ("an operation against the Karkosa"), `MCD-1654`, and `lauris-chronicle-lxviii-…md` line 68 ("aboard the Karkosa"), `lauris-chronicle-xxxvii` line 22 ("Karkosa's archive room").
  - **Conflicts with:** `GEO-001`/`GEO-003`/`MCD-110`/`MAW-060`/`WC-009`/`MCD-246`/`ARS-010` — Karkosa is the Sovereign Trust Domain's capital (Wallcrown City, G16), the Throat, the L1–L9 vertical complex in whose L9 vault the Trinity was sealed, and the target of Book 1's *Karkosa Heist* (`MCD-070`). # The Market That Rebuilt Itself

*Locked canon, Batch 200, 2026-09-11 (`MCD-822`). The Scourge Alias Chronicle XXXVII, wave 13 of the ten-wave sixth-through-fifteenth run. Not a territory Chronicle. Narrated in neutral third-person prose.*

---

The Varrow slaving hub had taken three months of patient surveillance and one decisive night to
dismantle entirely — every warehouse burned, every ledger seized, every buyer's name passed to a Trust
magistrate willing to act on it — and by every measure the crew's own records used to judge a
victory, it had been total.

A season later, a merchant sailing the same strait brought word that troubled him more than any
account of a fight lost ever had: the trade hadn't ended. It had simply moved forty miles down the
coast, rebuilt under new names, serving the exact same demand that had made Varrow profitable in the
first place, as though the hub itself had never been more than a convenient address for something far
harder to actually destroy.

"You burned the building," Efa Gol said, laying the report out plainly rather than
softening it. "You didn't burn the reason the building existed. That's a different fight, and I don't
think it's one the coat and the blade were ever built to win."

"Then what wins it?"

"I don't know that anything does, cleanly. Buyers keep buying as long as buying stays profitable
enough to be worth the risk. Every hub we burn just raises the price of the next one, and someone
always decides the price is still worth paying." She didn't offer comfort in the assessment,
only honesty. "You can keep making it expensive. You can't make it stop being wanted. That part isn't

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Batch 331: Phase 1.5 Atlas fable-review fixes (mechanical/reconciliation subset).

Applies the subset of the Atlas consistency review's findings that are pure
reconciliation against already-locked canon (no new creative/worldbuilding
facts): GEO-003's missing Rathaan Prime capital site, and GEO-006's
self-contradicting Hold/Settlement count wording against GEO-005.

The review's larger findings (C2 Verehimu/Voskharen Wetlands, C3 "aboard
the Karkosa", C5 the Teeth's placement, C6 MCD-094's area/population-weight
mismatch, E3 MCD-112's Southern Seaboard flag, and the EN1-EN9 enrichment
clusters -- Portside, the Kessic region, naval geography, Kesmara, House
Verehimu's seat, etc.) are new creative/worldbuilding decisions, not
reconciliation, and are deliberately NOT resolved here -- they remain
queued for Abad's own ruling, per the project's draft-then-approval
discipline.
"""
import json
from datetime import date

LEDGER_PATH = "canon-ledger.json"

SOURCE = (
    "Phase 1.5 fable-review of the World Atlas (GEO-001 through GEO-006) "
    "against the full Chronicle corpus and canon-ledger.json, following "
    "Phase 1's completion (Batches 320-330). Mechanical/reconciliation "
    "subset only."
)

AMENDMENTS = {
    "GEO-003": (
        "The atlas's canon-locked Capital/Maw sites, one per region: Rexhaven (Jicome), "
        "Ironmere (Aethel-Gard), The Spire (Zenith), Praetura/Maw-15 (The Prefecture), "
        "Kairo (The Shogunate), Skyvault (Astral Archipelago), Karkosa/The Throat "
        "(Sovereign Trust Domain), Ironhold plus Rathaan Prime and the Ash Maw Scar/"
        "Maw-1 Mother/Maw-3 Belly cluster (Lawless Reaches), Frontier Maw/Moonvault "
        "(Shattered Kingdoms), Dark Spire (T.D.K. Peninsula). Old Dominion Ruins has "
        "no canon-locked capital or Maw site -- fitting its fallen-civilization "
        "theming. Khorvane is a Hold within Old Dominion Ruins, not its capital; the "
        "earlier draft's naming of Khorvane as OD's capital is corrected here, per "
        "Abad's ruling that the live Atlas source controls over the earlier stale "
        "extraction. Corrected 2026-09-10 (Batch 103): the Karkosa capital venue is "
        "the unnumbered Throat (MAW-060); Maw-7 'the Keldane Maw'/'Slab of Judgment' "
        "(MAW-061) is a separate venue at Keldane, not Karkosa -- the earlier 'Maw-7 "
        "Slab' label for Karkosa was a stale pre-MAW-060/061 shorthand. Corrected "
        "2026-10-02 (Batch 331): the Lawless Reaches entry was missing Rathaan Prime "
        "(cell J20, Thornwork S), the live Atlas's fifth named Lawless Reaches "
        "Capital/Maw site and the Rathaan Federation's own seat (POL-090/POL-107)."
    ),
    "GEO-006": (
        "Beyond GEO-003's Capital/Maw roster, two Jicome-region sites carry "
        "Rebellion-era narrative weight and are locked here rather than left as "
        "free-to-rename flavor: Killane (Hold, Corehold-class fortress-city, cell "
        "C09, Jicome's southern district -- site of the Sewer War of Killane, "
        "MCD-234) and Ash Harbor (Settlement, Port-class, cell A09, Jicome's "
        "southern coast -- site of the Siege of the Ghost Harbor, MCD-235, "
        "informally renamed Ghost Harbor after the battle, per the Chronicle's own "
        "in-story renaming; grows to city scale over the Long Mask era, MCD-1352). "
        "With these two canon-locked additions the Gazetteer's Hold/Settlement total "
        "becomes 54 (24 Holds, 30 Settlements), of which GEO-005's 52 remain free to "
        "rename -- corrected 2026-10-02 (Batch 331) to resolve a wording "
        "contradiction between GEO-005 and this rule over whether the 52 included or "
        "excluded these two sites; they are, and always were, excluded from the "
        "free-to-rename 52 and additional to it."
    ),
}


def main():
    with open(LEDGER_PATH) as f:
        ledger = json.load(f)

    rules_by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in ledger["rules"]}

    amended = []
    for rid, new_statement in AMENDMENTS.items():
        assert rid in rules_by_id, f"missing rule {rid}"
        rules_by_id[rid]["statement"] = new_statement
        amended.append(rid)

    ids = [r["id"] for r in ledger["rules"]]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "duplicate rule IDs found"

    next_batch = max(b["batch"] for b in ledger["batches_completed"]) + 1
    ledger["batches_completed"].append({
        "batch": next_batch,
        "date": str(date.today()),
        "source": SOURCE,
        "rule_count": 0,
        "note": (
            "Phase 1.5 Atlas fable-review, mechanical subset. Amends GEO-003 (adds "
            "the missing Rathaan Prime capital site to the Lawless Reaches entry) "
            "and GEO-006 (resolves a GEO-005/GEO-006 wording contradiction over "
            "whether Killane/Ash Harbor are included in or additional to the 52 "
            "free-to-rename Holds/Settlements -- they are additional). Also fixes, "
            "prose-only (no ledger-statement change needed): a Kessic-region "
            "collision in two Bane Chronicles (MCD-681/683, the rumor's "
            "never-visited location renamed 'the Brinemoor salt flats' to resolve a "
            "contradiction with Kanja's own directly-established Kessic history); a "
            "second near-collision in a Scourge Chronicle (MCD-822, 'Varrow' renamed "
            "'Callow' to resolve a one-letter collision with the already-locked "
            "antagonist Lord Varro Dominael); and a real-world proper-noun leak "
            "('COINTELPRO') in Sankofa Chronicle V's narrative prose (MCD-1025), "
            "reworded to plain descriptive prose. The review's larger findings -- "
            "the Verehimu/Voskharen Wetlands naming question, whether 'the Karkosa' "
            "is the crew's own base or the enemy capital, the Teeth's Atlas "
            "placement, MCD-094's area-vs-population-weight framing, MCD-112's "
            "Southern Seaboard flag, and a full Portside/Kessic-region/naval-"
            "geography/Kesmara/House-Verehimu-seat enrichment pass -- are new "
            "creative/worldbuilding decisions, not reconciliation, and remain "
            "queued for Abad's own ruling rather than resolved here."
        ),
    })

    old_version = float(ledger["ledger_version"])
    ledger["ledger_version"] = str(round(old_version + 0.1, 1))
    ledger["last_updated"] = str(date.today())

    with open(LEDGER_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump(ledger, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write("\n")

    print(
        f"OK: {len(ledger['rules'])} total rules, {len(ledger['batches_completed'])} "
        f"batches, ledger_version {ledger['ledger_version']}, zero duplicate IDs. "
        f"{len(amended)} rule statements amended: {', '.join(amended)}."
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Batch 332: Phase 2 fable-review fixes, Ezio Valcari Character Chronicle material.

Mechanical/reconciliation fixes only. Amends ARS-404's rule statement to
remove a real-world-term leak ("the way a doctor reads an X-ray"). All
other findings from the review were either applied as prose-only
corrections to the one locked Chronicle file (MCD-1876, no ledger
statement change needed) and to the three still-UNLOCKED/PENDING-APPROVAL
draft Chronicles II-IV (corrected for internal consistency but NOT
locked -- they remain pending Abad's own approval), or are flagged in
CLAUDE.md as needing Abad's direct creative ruling (Ezio's true age
against CC-028; whether Fermand is a sixth knower of Ezio's classified
capability).
"""
import json
from datetime import date

LEDGER_PATH = "canon-ledger.json"

SOURCE = (
    "Phase 2 fable-review of Ezio Valcari's Character Chronicle material "
    "(his profile doc, CC-073, MCD-1875, MCD-1876, CC-156, and the three "
    "pending-approval Chronicles II-IV) against the full ledger. "
    "Mechanical/reconciliation subset only."
)

AMENDMENTS = {
    "ARS-404": (
        "Extends ARS-210 (that entry's Attia's Rite/cane-sword listing for Ezio "
        "remains superseded in favor of Lauris per ARS-359 and is not restated "
        "here): the Archive-Key is a set of twelve hair-thin Living Drakma "
        "filaments, bio-tuned to Ezio's own resonance, housed in the hollow shaft "
        "of the Cipher Cane -- a plain, unremarkable cane that reads publicly as a "
        "theorist's affectation, privately as his only concealed-carry prop, "
        "distinct from and never confused with Attia's Rite. The filaments defeat "
        "locks and mechanisms by touch-reading their internal structure through "
        "micro-vibration feedback -- he identifies the correct configuration by "
        "feel, the way a trained hand reads structure through touch alone, then "
        "shapes a filament to match it. A secondary function lets the filaments "
        "interface directly with Directorate Drakma data-plates, reading sealed "
        "classified SBD records back to him as touch-interpreted micro-vibration. "
        "Structural Interrogation -- mapping a room's density and structure in two "
        "taps -- is performed with the same Cipher Cane."
    ),
}


def main():
    with open(LEDGER_PATH) as f:
        ledger = json.load(f)

    rules_by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in ledger["rules"]}

    amended = []
    for rid, new_statement in AMENDMENTS.items():
        assert rid in rules_by_id, f"missing rule {rid}"
        rules_by_id[rid]["statement"] = new_statement
        amended.append(rid)

    ids = [r["id"] for r in ledger["rules"]]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "duplicate rule IDs found"

    next_batch = max(b["batch"] for b in ledger["batches_completed"]) + 1
    ledger["batches_completed"].append({
        "batch": next_batch,
        "date": str(date.today()),
        "source": SOURCE,
        "rule_count": 0,
        "note": (
            "Phase 2 fable-review of Ezio Valcari's Character Chronicle material. "
            "Amends ARS-404 to remove a real-world-term leak ('the way a doctor "
            "reads an X-ray') from its rule statement. Also fixed, prose-only (no "
            "ledger-statement change needed): MCD-1876's own locked Chronicle I "
            "file (a settlement-count contradiction reconciled to three "
            "throughout; a dangling numeric age claim reworded pending Abad's "
            "ruling on Ezio's true age; two cosmetic fixes); and internal-"
            "consistency fixes to the three still-unlocked/pending-approval draft "
            "Chronicles II-IV (dangling numeric spans reworded, an incorrect "
            "header claim about Lauris Chronicle I corrected, a CC-108 overstatement "
            "softened) -- these three drafts remain UNLOCKED/PENDING APPROVAL, not "
            "locked by this batch. The profile doc's three different Industrial "
            "Myth appearance counts (84/31/35) were clarified in place with one "
            "defining sentence rather than changed, since all three measure "
            "genuinely different things. Two findings require Abad's own direct "
            "creative ruling and are deliberately left unresolved: Ezio's true age "
            "(CC-028's '75 years old' is contradicted by MCD-373's placement of "
            "him at roughly age 16 at the Furnace District Strike, which implies "
            "roughly 309 at Book 1, and by MCD-194/MCD-1661's two-centuries-old "
            "Lauris-recruitment arrangement); and whether Fermand Aurelias is a "
            "sixth knower of Ezio's classified combat capability (pending "
            "Chronicle IV's dialogue reads as telling him, in tension with its "
            "own header and Chronicle III's header, both of which assert he stays "
            "outside the closed five-person list -- WC-016/CC-027/CC-111)."
        ),
    })

    old_version = float(ledger["ledger_version"])
    ledger["ledger_version"] = str(round(old_version + 0.1, 1))
    ledger["last_updated"] = str(date.today())

    with open(LEDGER_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump(ledger, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write("\n")

    print(
        f"OK: {len(ledger['rules'])} total rules, {len(ledger['batches_completed'])} "
        f"batches, ledger_version {ledger['ledger_version']}, zero duplicate IDs. "
        f"{len(amended)} rule statements amended: {', '.join(amended)}."
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	# Daba Chronicle LIII: What a Quiet Year Looks Like
     2	
     3	*Locked canon, Batch 315, 2026-09-28. Daba Chronicle LIII, third entry of the next-wave sweep, closing it.
     4	Close-third on Daba, no dedicated narrator. Deliberately a pure texture entry — no plot advance, no
     5	threat, and no touch on `MCD-1569`'s unspecified Book 1 trigger — showing what the network's
     6	"running semi-dormant" present actually looks like day to day. Reuses Kether, Wrenna, Deryn Kettel,
     7	and Tessin. No new named characters.*
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	Nothing happened, and that was the entire point of the year, and Daba spent the better part of an
    12	autumn morning proving it to himself the only way he knew how: by walking the network's own ledger
    13	from one end to the other and finding, entry after entry, that the ledger had almost nothing left to
    14	say.
    15	
    16	Kether ran the recruitment vetting now, mostly, the eleven-day watches Daba had once done personally
    17	compressed by her own refinements into something closer to seven, a change she'd defended to him two
    18	years ago with the same numerically grounded case she'd once made for scaling the network up
    19	entirely — a case he had, once again, only half accepted, granting the shorter timeline while
    20	insisting the depth of the watch itself stay unchanged. He reviewed her latest three candidates over
    21	breakfast, found nothing in her notes he would have caught and she hadn't, and told her so, which was,
    22	between them, its own established language: he did not offer praise easily, and she had long since
    23	learned that his silence where a correction should have been was the only compliment he gave.
    24	
    25	Tessin, a full three years past the anniversary of her own vetting's end, ran two cells now instead
    26	of one, and had developed, without anyone teaching her to, a habit of leaving her own private note in
    27	the margin of every report she filed — not operational content, just a single line marking how the
    28	day had actually felt to live through, a practice Daba had noticed months ago and deliberately never
    29	mentioned, because it was hers, built without his instruction, and he had learned the hard way that
    30	the things people built for themselves without being told to build them were the ones that mattered
    31	most and needed the least of his own hand near them.
    32	
    33	Deryn Kettel spent the morning re-shoeing a courier's horse in the network's third safehouse stable, a
    34	task that had nothing to do with tactics or doctrine or the count of anything, and Daba found him
    35	there at midday and sat on an overturned bucket and watched her work for the better part of an hour
    36	without either of them saying much, because some silences between two people who had survived things
    37	together didn't need filling.
    38	
    39	Tessin — the recruit who'd nearly cost the effort a wavering candidate years ago, who'd since become
    40	one of the network's most careful teachers of exactly the caution his own early mistake had taught
    41	him — spent the afternoon walking a new intake through the same lesson Daba had once walked Kanja
    42	through at a drainage cut a lifetime ago: a road is not a road if nobody watches it, and a habit is
    43	the most dangerous unguarded door in any district. Daba listened from the doorway of the training
    44	room without correcting a single word, because Tessin had earned, through the specific arithmetic of
    45	having made the mistake and survived being corrected for it, the right to teach the lesson exactly as
    46	he understood it, in his own words, and Daba's own presence in the doorway was, by design, the whole
    47	of his contribution.
    48	
    49	He walked the annual list that evening, alone, in the small back room he kept for exactly this
    50	purpose and no other. Fennic's name. The one thousand eight hundred and four. The names added since,
    51	few now, fewer each year, the network's own doctrine of extreme patience finally paying the interest
    52	it had always promised rather than merely accruing it. He read every name aloud, the way he had every
    53	year since the first, and closed the book without adding anything new to it, because there was
    54	nothing new to add, and he let himself, for exactly as long as it took to close the cover and set it
    55	back on its shelf, feel the specific, unfamiliar weight of a ledger that had held still for a while.
    56	
    57	It would not hold still forever. He knew that the way he knew tide charts and drainage angles — not
    58	as a fear, just as a fact the doctrine itself was built to survive. Something, someday, would ask the
    59	network what it had all been for, in a register louder than Tessin's own quiet question at a closing
    60	meal, and he did not know what that something would be, or when, and had long since stopped needing
    61	to know before he was willing to keep building toward whatever it turned out to require.
    62	
    63	For now, though, there was a horse re-shod, a candidate vetted, a lesson taught by the right teacher,
    64	a margin note written by a woman who'd never been told to write one, and a list that had gone a full
    65	year without a new name in it.
    66	
    67	He locked the back room, walked out past Kether's own quiet nod, past Tessin's cell reports stacked
    68	neat on the front table, past the stable where Deryn Kettel was still working, past the training room
    69	where Perrin's voice carried on, patient, thorough, unhurried, and went to find Mika, because a
    70	quiet year, he had decided somewhere in the last hour without quite noticing the decision arrive, was
    71	exactly the kind of year a man might, for once, allow himself to spend some of on a house with a
    72	window that faced the water.
    73	
    74	He did not go that night either. But he thought, for the first time, that he might.
    75	
    76	---
    77	
    78	*Continuity notes (not narrative): deliberately no threat, no plot advance, and no reference to
    79	`MCD-1569`'s unspecified Book 1 trigger anywhere in the entry — pure texture showing the network's
    80	mature, semi-dormant operational present. Closes the three-entry wave on a soft callback to
    81	Chronicle LI's still-unresolved house/Mika thread (deliberately not resolved here either — "he did
    82	not go... but he thought, for the first time, that he might" is forward motion, not closure). No new
    83	named characters — Kether, Wrenna, Deryn Kettel, and Tessin all reused from the existing corpus
    84	(Kether from Chronicle XXXIX, Wrenna from Chronicles XXIX/L, Deryn Kettel and Tessin from Batch 296's
    85	cross-block collision-sweep renames).*

text:
"You don't mind that he gets remembered and you don't."

"I don't mind that he gets remembered. I built this whole life on the principle that being remembered
and being effective are, past a certain size, opposites. I chose the second one on purpose, before I
ever met him, for reasons that had nothing to do with him at all." Daba looked out at the dark tree
line, unremarkable, doing exactly the job it had been chosen for. "What I sit with, some evenings, isn't
envy. It's a stranger thing. It's that the boy I taught used to need everyone he lost written down by
name, so none of them went into a ledger as a number -- I watched that need get built in him before he
ever met me, at a table with a woman and a ledger, a story that isn't mine to tell in full. And the life
I've built since is the exact opposite of that need. Nobody in 1804 goes into any ledger at all, by
name or by number, if I've done my work correctly. The safest thing I can do for every person under my
protection is make sure no record of them exists anywhere a stranger could ever find it." He exhaled,
something between a laugh and its absence. "I have spent my whole adult life perfecting the one thing
the boy I loved as a son once told me, without knowing he was telling me anything, that he could never
forgive if it were done to the people he lost. I don't think it's a contradiction. I think it's just
what the work actually costs, when you look at it honestly instead of at the doctrine that makes it
sound clean."

Perrin was quiet for a while. "And the reward," he said finally. "You said there was one. You always
say there's one."
