*Locked canon, Batch 296, 2026-09-18 (`MCD-1581`). Entry 11 of 50 in Daba's own Chronicle series,
launched under the Character Chronicle Gameplan's own protagonist-series model. Dramatizes first
contact between Daba and a young, not-yet-Rebellion-era Kanja, during the "otherwise-unrecorded
formative years" `MCD-1568` establishes -- a scene of raw, uninstructed instinct (`MCD-311`) seen
from outside for the first time, and the mutual wariness before any trust exists between them. Abad's
approval: "rate 50 Chronicles in batches using as many agents as needed to make it efficient." Corrected Batch 335, 2026-10-02: "twenty years" softened to "years" (1804 is only a few years old at this point in the mentorship); "Corrow" renamed "Sarrow" to resolve a collision with the already-locked Bane-track "Corrow ravine network." *

---
===
# Daba Chronicle LIII: What a Quiet Year Looks Like

*Locked canon, Batch 315, 2026-09-28. Daba Chronicle LIII, third entry of the next-wave sweep, closing it.
Close-third on Daba, no dedicated narrator. Deliberately a pure texture entry — no plot advance, no
threat, and no touch on `MCD-1569`'s unspecified Book 1 trigger — showing what the network's
"running semi-dormant" present actually looks like day to day. Reuses Kether, Tessin, Deryn Kettel,
and Perrin. No new named characters. Corrected Batch 335, 2026-10-02: "Wrenna" renamed "Tessin" throughout; a separate male "Tessin" paragraph (an invented backstory that didn't exist elsewhere in Daba's corpus, and cross-contaminated from a different character's own plot) was rewritten to feature Perrin instead; Deryn Kettel's pronouns corrected to she/her, matching Chronicle XLI's own established usage. *

---
Good, correctly formed. Now let me also fix the EN3/EN4 profile doc notes and write the Daba merge script for the ledger-level amendments (MCD-1581, 1613, 1870, 1871, 1873, 1874).

=== MCD-1581 ===
Daba Chronicle XI, "The Boy Who Broke the Scaffold" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/daba-chronicle-xi-the-boy-who-broke-the-scaffold.md), the eleventh entry in Daba's own Chronicle series and the launch wave's first-contact entry. During Kanja's otherwise-unrecorded formative years (MCD-1568), a 1804 scout, Riasa Vorn (a new named character, collision-checked clean), reports a young Kanja dismantling three Trust enforcers at the Corrow ore-cut using nothing but a structural read of a collapsing ore-basket scaffold -- pure uninstructed Rexmar instinct per MCD-311, causing no deaths. Daba investigates personally and confronts the boy at the ruined scaffold; both recognize the other as dangerous and unknown, and the entry closes on deliberate mutual wariness rather than any trust, establishing the state the mentorship must still be built from. New named character: Riasa Vorn.

=== MCD-1613 ===
Daba Chronicle XLIII, "What the Smoke Never Touched" (full narrative text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/daba-chronicle-xliii-what-the-smoke-never-touched.md), the forty-third entry in Daba's own Chronicle series. Pursuing an unrelated forgery case, Daba and lieutenant Elowen Marn (new named character) pass within sight of the already-locked Furnace District Strike (MCD-244, age 21) from a ridge overlooking the smelting district; Daba recognizes the unnamed unarmed figure below without naming him aloud, judges correctly that the standoff will not turn violent, and deliberately withdraws south with his own escort rather than approach, letting the strike resolve entirely on its own. Dramatizes 1804 operating near but never within one of Kanja's own campaigns, honoring MCD-1569's "never folded into" constraint without altering that battle's own locked participant account. New minor named character Elowen Marn, collision-checked clean.

=== MCD-1870 ===
Daba Chronicle LII, 'The Ground That Almost Wasn't Enough' (full text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/daba-chronicle-lii-the-ground-that-almost-wasnt-enough.md). Second entry of the wave -- the first Chronicle in the entire 53-entry corpus to put Daba's S-tier rating (CC-135) under genuine physical threat, since he holds no variant biology or density scaling and his rating comes entirely from guerrilla mastery and tactical discipline. Closing a safehouse at Threnfall personally after it is traced by a patient, unnamed Trust Compliance captain and eleven enforcers, Daba survives only by applying his own core doctrine (density is not power if the terrain neutralizes it, MCD-1567/1568) to save his own life for the first time, escaping through a disused well and drainage culvert rather than confronting the perimeter directly. He is genuinely wounded -- an injury decided by luck, not skill, the first time in his own life that distinction has applied -- and is saved on arrival at a second safehouse by Wrenna's counting-as-containment response, a discipline he built into her without ever fully explaining why. Reuses Bren and Wrenna. No new named characters; the antagonist captain and his enforcers are deliberately unnamed. Does not touch or dramatize the separate, still-undramatized Harek Vondel defeat reserved at MCD-1855.

=== MCD-1871 ===
Daba Chronicle LIII, 'What a Quiet Year Looks Like' (full text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/daba-chronicle-liii-what-a-quiet-year-looks-like.md). Third entry of the wave, closing it -- a deliberate pure-texture entry with no threat and no plot advance, showing 1804's mature, semi-dormant present day to day: Kether's refined seven-day recruit vetting, Wrenna running two cells and keeping an unprompted personal margin-note habit in her reports, Deryn Kettel's ordinary stable work, and Tessin teaching a new intake the same terrain-as-weapon lesson Daba once taught Kanja. Daba reads his annual list of names aloud and finds nothing new to add to it for the first time in years, a rare quiet accounting. Closes on a soft, deliberately unresolved callback to Chronicle LI's still-open house/Mika thread -- he does not go that night either, but for the first time thinks he might. Reuses Kether, Wrenna, Deryn Kettel, and Tessin. No new named characters. Does not name or imply MCD-1569's unspecified Book 1 trigger for 1804.

=== MCD-1873 ===
Daba Chronicle LV, 'The Name Daba Never Spoke' (full text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/daba-chronicle-lv-the-name-daba-never-spoke.md). Second entry of the wave. Prompted directly by his own near-death at Threnfall (MCD-1870), Daba confronts a structural gap he had never applied to himself: 1804's blind-succession doctrine (locked at MCD-1597, Yeva Tolan/Marn) protects every cell's leadership against capture or loss except his own. Over three weeks he extends the same structure to the network's own top for the first time, choosing Kether as his unwitting successor through the identical method used elsewhere -- small, unexplained authority handed over on ordinary days, culminating in giving her unsupervised access to the annual list's back room. Kether does not learn she has been chosen, and does not learn the true margin of Threnfall's danger either, matching the doctrine's own stated logic (a second who watches her leader for signs of the next near-miss is already half doing the job before she's needed). Reuses Kether, Bren, and Wrenna. No new named characters.

=== MCD-1874 ===
Daba Chronicle LVI, 'What Vetting Cannot See' (full text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/daba-chronicle-lvi-what-vetting-cannot-see.md). Third entry of the wave, closing it -- the corpus's first genuine doctrine-limit entry for the vetting mechanism itself. Sarel Doune, a courier who passed 1804's full year-long vetting faithfully and shows no malice or carelessness, mentions a safehouse's approximate location to her own sister in an ordinary, loving family conversation; the fragment travels through two further unrelated conversations before landing, by pure administrative bad luck, unread in the wrong Trust district and causing no actual harm. Tracing the chain, Daba concludes the vetting doctrine (MCD-1567) has a real, permanent hole it cannot close -- it tests for resistance under deliberate pressure but has no method for a person's ordinary, ungovernable love for someone never vetted at all, and closing that hole would mean punishing the exact quality that makes a person trustworthy in the first place. He does not tell Sarel, judging that the fear it would create would cost more than the risk itself, and files the fact as a permanently unresolved, unaudited cost of the network's own safety rather than a problem to be solved. New named character Sarel Doune, collision-checked clean. Reuses Kether. No new other named characters; no child-safety issues.
Now writing the merge script with all six ledger-statement amendments.

        "(MCD-244, age 21) from a ridge overlooking the smelting district; Daba "
        "recognizes the unnamed unarmed figure below without naming him aloud, "
        "judges correctly that the standoff will not turn violent, and deliberately "
        "withdraws south with his own escort rather than approach, letting the "
        "strike resolve entirely on its own -- the strike itself runs the already-"
        "locked eleven days (MCD-244), not the two this entry's prose originally "
        "misstated. Dramatizes 1804 operating near but never within one of Kanja's "
        "own campaigns, honoring MCD-1569's \"never folded into\" constraint without "
        "altering that battle's own locked participant account. New minor named "

def main():

        rules_by_id[rid]["statement"] = new_statement

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Batch 338: Phase 3 fable-review fixes, the Kanja-version Chronicle track.

Amends MCD-1865 (an anachronistic post-Breach custodial-authority
reference, decades before the Great Breach that actually occurs at the
age this defeat is locked) and MCD-1588 (a stale "nine years prior"
figure the Batch 335 Daba prose fix corrected to "three years ago" but
never propagated to this rule's own statement).
"""
import json
from datetime import date

LEDGER_PATH = "canon-ledger.json"

SOURCE = (
    "Phase 3 fable-review of the Kanja-version Chronicle track (Chronicles "
    "I-III, MCD-1866-1868) against the full ledger and corpus."
)

AMENDMENTS = {
    "MCD-1865": (
        "Renfel Auberon (CC-157) is eventually cornered and his contained "
        "Ever-Haunt stock safely neutralized by a coordinated application of "
        "CULT-197's own named three-source Anti-Resonance countermeasure -- "
        "Onyx's Cadence Ruin, Sephtis's Chrono-Anchor bells, and Ironbane's King's "
        "Roar -- fielded together for the first time on the page against a real "
        "threat rather than described only as a standing procedure, forcing every "
        "entity in Auberon's custody to flee or collapse to its lowest tier rather "
        "than be harmed outright. Auberon himself is captured alive rather than "
        "killed: years of unsafe proximity to his own 'merchandise' have already "
        "left him partially Green-Mark-contaminated (CULT-198), making him more a "
        "cautionary case than a mastermind, and he is handed to the older "
        "custodial apparatus that already tracks anomalies of this kind (the "
        "defeat sits at age 27, MCD-1868, well before the Great Breach) rather "
        "than to ordinary Trust law enforcement. Chronicle prose drafted Batch "
        "313 (MCD-1868)."
    ),
    "MCD-1588": (
        "Daba Chronicle XVIII, \"The Weight a Crossing Cannot Carry\" (full narrative "
        "text at docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/daba-chronicle-xviii-the-weight-a-"
        "crossing-cannot-carry.md), the eighteenth entry in Daba's own Chronicle "
        "series. Dramatizes the discipline of making concentrated force irrelevant "
        "via a recounted (not restaged) 1804 operation three years prior: eight of "
        "Daba's fighters narrowed a forty-one-strong Trust ford crossing with "
        "submerged stake lines to three men abreast, ensuring only six soldiers "
        "could ever be engaged at once regardless of the column's total size, "
        "taking twelve losses before the rest of the column understood the water "
        "itself was refusing them reinforcement. Explicitly the most direct "
        "conceptual ancestor of Kanja's own later Dredge-Line Ambush (MCD-231). No "
        "new named characters."
    ),
}


def main():
    with open(LEDGER_PATH) as f:
        ledger = json.load(f)

    rules_by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in ledger["rules"]}

    amended = []
    for rid, new_statement in AMENDMENTS.items():
        assert rid in rules_by_id, f"missing rule {rid}"
        rules_by_id[rid]["statement"] = new_statement
        amended.append(rid)

    ids = [r["id"] for r in ledger["rules"]]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "duplicate rule IDs found"

    next_batch = max(b["batch"] for b in ledger["batches_completed"]) + 1
    ledger["batches_completed"].append({
        "batch": next_batch,
        "date": str(date.today()),
        "source": SOURCE,
        "rule_count": 0,
        "note": (
            "Phase 3 fable-review of the Kanja-version Chronicle track (3 "
            "entries, Chronicles I-III). Amends MCD-1865 (its 'post-Breach "
            "anomalies' custodial-authority phrasing was anachronistic -- the "
            "Great Breach doesn't occur until Book 1's epilogue, decades after "
            "this defeat's own locked age-27 placement at MCD-1868; also records "
            "that Chronicle prose now exists) and MCD-1588 (a stale 'nine years "
            "prior' figure the Batch 335 Daba prose fix corrected to 'three years "
            "ago' in the Chronicle file itself but never propagated to this "
            "rule's own statement). Also fixed, prose-only: Chronicle III's "
            "header mis-dated the Gale Straits by two years and gave Sephtis an "
            "age roughly 200 years too old (stale age-arithmetic, same error "
            "class as the Lauris sweep); an entity-count arithmetic error (2+3+2 "
            "summed to seven, not six); Chronicle I's Scrip-Forge wage-shortfall "
            "dialogue conflated a 14%-content note with a 14% shortfall against "
            "its 38% stamp, corrected to state both figures; Chronicle II's "
            "header age specificity loosened from 'fifteenth year' to "
            "'seventeenth year' to match the only locked constraint (before "
            "Onyx's age-17 bonding) rather than an unforced tighter pin; a "
            "garbled line of dialogue punctuation fixed. The profile doc "
            "(kanja-haku-rexmar.md) had six stale/garbled lines corrected: the "
            "founding crew's CC- dossier gap (now filled, CC-158/159/160); the "

the six years of a hundred small debts and a hundred small kindnesses that made the hall worth
occupying in the first place — and they saved each other, in an order that looked rehearsed because

exactly as someone had once, patiently, unhurriedly, taught them to.

Fourth Kazi territory Chronicle"), `MCD-1529` ("fifth"), `MCD-1530` ("sixth"), `MCD-1531` ("seventh"), `MCD-1532` ("eighth"); and the matching header lines of Kazi IX–XIII files (line 3 of each: "Fourth/Fifth/Sixth/Seventh/Eighth entry in Kazi's own Chronicles") plus each file's closing continuity-note sentence.
  - **Problem:** The Femi agent drafted in parallel with the Tunji agent and never saw Chronicles IV–VIII (`MCD-1523`–`1527`, which correctly call themselves fourth through eighth). Chronicles IX–XIII are the ninth through thirteenth entries. Two sets of rules now both claim "fourth through eighth."
  - **Fix (mechanical):** In `MCD-1528`: `the fourth entry` → `the ninth entry`; `Fourth Kazi territory Chronicle` → `Ninth Kazi territory Chronicle`. `MCD-1529`: `fifth entry` → `tenth entry`; `Fifth Kazi` → `Tenth Kazi`. `MCD-1530`: `sixth` → `eleventh` (both places). `MCD-1531`: `seventh` → `twelfth` (both). `MCD-1532`: `eighth` → `thirteenth` (both). Apply the identical substitutions to each file's header (line 3) and its continuity-note closing sentence (IX line 69–70, X line 68, XI line 73, XII line 79, XIII line 65). Re-sync the five Drive docs.
  
  ### E2. Kazi VIII misattributes the docked-pay incident (rank and season)
  - **File:** Kazi VIII lines 30–32 ("the plant manager who'd docked three men's pay over his own scheduling error, the same manager from the gantry season").
  - **Problem:** The only docked-pay-over-his-own-scheduling-error incident in the corpus is Kazi IV lines 32–36, committed by **a line supervisor**, months *before* Chronicle I — not "the gantry season" (Chronicle V, which is months after IV and involves a *plant manager* only as the person who arrives to hear the demand). VIII fuses the two. Same error class as the Dol Maren/Maret Vos trait-bleed fixed in Batch 226/320.
  - **Fix (mechanical):** Kazi VIII line 31–32: `the plant manager who'd docked three men's pay over his own scheduling error, the same manager from the gantry season, still unpunished` → `the line supervisor who'd docked three men's pay over his own scheduling error, back before the gantry walkout, still unpunished`. No ledger change (MCD-1527 doesn't carry the detail).

  - **File:** `kiti-chronicle-iii-...md` line 18 ("the same patient deliberation he'd once brought to every obstruction he'd worn down over the years").

"The Long Tenure" (`PH2-059`) is the inverse: attrition *against him* fails; it is explicitly "purely defensive" and "does nothing to expand his reach." Minor cross-territory ability-bleed in characterization prose.
  - **Fix (mechanical):** `every obstruction he'd worn down over the years` → `every attrition campaign he'd outlasted over the years`.
  
  ### E4. Category-tag drift across Kazi's own 13 rules (and the tracks generally)
  - **Rules:** MCD-351 = `World Mechanics`; MCD-363 = `phase2-homage-chronicle`; MCD-523 = `phase2-territory-chronicle`; MCD-1523–1527 = `territory-chronicle`; MCD-1528–1532 = `phase2-homage-chronicle`. Across all 71 territory-Chronicle rules corpus-wide the split is `phase2-territory-chronicle` 32 / `World Mechanics` 17 / `phase2-homage-chronicle` 12 / `territory-chronicle` 10.
  - **Problem:** Same class as the `MCD-365` and `MCD-1730` category fixes already applied in prior phases. Not a canon fact, but any chunk-selection or archive-app query by category is lossy (the pilot already noted category+name is unreliable).
  - **Fix (mechanical, optional, orchestrator's call):** normalize all 71 to the plurality value `phase2-territory-chronicle`. If the orchestrator prefers to leave categories alone, at minimum note that MCD-351 through MCD-355 carrying `World Mechanics` is the worst mismatch.

  - **Rule:** `PH2-051` still reads "Two lieutenants ... stand as his founding co-organizers, not yet individually named or detailed." Superseded by `PH2-063`/`PH2-064` (Batch 100) and extended by `PH2-065`/`PH2-066` (Batch 287).
  - **Fix (mechanical, matches the project's in-place-amendment precedent for PH2-021/030):** replace that clause with `stand as his founding co-organizers -- Kunle (PH2-063) and Kalamu (PH2-064); his in-plant organizing partner Tunji (PH2-065) and trustee-seat holder Femi (PH2-066) were added in Batch 287.`

  ---

  ### D1. "Torvald" vs. the homage-era naming convention (PH2-034)
  - **Files:** Kazi V (`MCD-1524`), Kazi VIII (`MCD-1527`).
  - Torvald is Old Norse. `PH2-034` is a standing rule that homage-era names "draw from real Taino, Yoruba, Akan, Kikongo, Nahuatl, Swahili, or other real Black/brown-diasporic vocabulary." The collision check itself held (zero hits outside the two Kazi files). Two readings: (a) an oversight by the drafting agent, fixable by a rename in both files + both rule statements; (b) a deliberate choice — the real Dodge Main floor was mixed, and Torvald being the hire who folds first could be read as intentional. Since PH2-034 is categorical and this is the only non-palette name across all 25 Detroit files, I'd recommend asking.   ### D2. Whether PH2-055 / PH2-053 / PH2-059 should be amended in place to absorb their Chronicle-locked extensions
  - Hekalu III (`MCD-525`) locks that "The Common Table" **requires periodic renewal** — `PH2-055` still says the network "quietly enforces itself" with no duration clause. The project has amended PH2 cards in place before (PH2-021, PH2-030). Abad's call whether to fold them in; if yes, append one cross-referencing sentence per card, no new facts.

Printed newspapers/"newspaperman" (Kazi VIII, Kiti I) are covered by `PH2-064`'s locked "printed sheets" and need no change.

  ## VERIFIED CLEAN (no finding)
  
  - **Grace Lee Boggs partner (Nyansa):** never named, never given an invented name, never even referenced on-page in any of the three Nyansa files. The one female character in the corpus (Nyansa III's "younger organizer," she/her) is clearly a junior colleague, not the life partner. Clean — the deliberate-omission rule holds.
  - **Real-world proper nouns in narrative prose:** zero across all 25 files. Every real-name hit (Watson, Hamlin, Cockrel, Grace Lee Boggs) sits only in italic header/continuity notes as research anchors, exactly per PH2-034.
  - **Writers'-room leaks in prose:** none. No rule IDs, batch numbers, "wave" references, or Voice-Bible labels inside narrative text in any file.
  - **Unnamed-Kanja convention:** holds in all 25 entries. Kanja speaks in Taifa I, Hekalu I (silent), Nyansa I, Kiti I — all within the established dialogue-permitted range; never named, never commands, never credited. Kazi VII's porch-step boy and Kazi X's archive-mover ("at Femi's own quiet request") are the most active, both within precedent (Borikén I carrying people; Kwan I shielding a marcher).
  - **Pronouns:** consistent for every named character across every appearance — Zola (she, 4 files), Adaeze (she), Torvald/Juma/Bakari/Kunle/Kalamu/Tunji/Femi/Irin/Osei/Yaw/Adom/Adisa/Owusu (he), Owusu's chief aide (she, Kiti II; unpronouned in III).
  - **Proper-noun collisions:** Zola, Juma, Torvald, Adaeze, Bakari, Kunle, Kalamu, Tunji, Femi, Irin, Osei, Yaw, Adom, Adisa, Owusu all return hits only inside their own track (plus `MCD-1855`/`daba.md`, which merely cite "Batch 287 (Tunji/Femi)" as a *process* precedent, not a character crossover — clean). No cross-world bleed of Daba/1804 names into Kazi or vice versa.
  - **"The Line Stops" limit (PH2-051):** respected throughout — Kazi I (outside hires feel nothing), II (Irin states it can't catch one man isolated), III (dock gangs generalization requires genuine interdependence), XI/XIII (Irin never tries the halt against institutional isolation of Femi), XII (finishing section explicitly measured as bound before the call).
  - **"Kin at a Distance" sincerity (PH2-053):** Taifa I/II/III consistent; "three cities," "a hundred sworn," "distance has never mattered" all stable across entries.
  - **"The Common Table" free choice (PH2-055):** Hekalu I/II/III consistent; II's "unrelated rival owner" correctly distinguishes the spy's boss from I's bonded owner; III's "years" after II's "months" chains correctly.
  - **"The Long Correction" (PH2-057):** Nyansa I/II/III consistent; II's "months before" and III's "years" chain correctly.
  - **"The Long Tenure" (PH2-059):** Kiti I → II → III chain correctly (apart from C5/E3 above); III's permanent lapse on resignation matches PH2-059's "lapses completely the moment he is out of office."
  - **Kazi internal timeline (after applying C3):** IV (pre-I, months) → I → II (+11 days, trial +9) → V/VI/VIII (V ≥ months after IV; VI after II and after V; VIII 3 months after V) → IX (post-I) → X (+1 month) → XI (~1 year) → XII → XIII (year 2). Tunji's age arithmetic in VII (31, raised from 9, "twenty-two years") checks. Bakari-as-student in VI correctly follows his trial in II.
  - Taifa I's planted hook ("something the stranger would not fully understand until considerably later, from a source other than Osei himself") is still unpaid after II and III — not an error, noted under enrichment.
  
  ---
  
  ## ENRICHMENT
  
  1. **Taifa:** the Chronicle I hook above (what Osei's face did at "the ones who didn't [swear]") is the strongest unpaid thread in the Detroit set — natural candidate for a Taifa IV about Yaw, or about the backstory-only exiled first president, without naming him.
  2. **Hekalu:** Adom's "own second" (Hekalu II) is the only recurring unnamed lieutenant in the Detroit set; Hekalu is the thinnest supporting cast of the five (zero named figures beyond Adom). A named second, built on the Shrine's real cooperative-economics institutions (the press, the farms — both in `PH2-054`), would mirror what Batch 287 did for Kazi.
  3. **Nyansa:** Nyansa III's "younger organizer" (she) is a ready-made second-generation figure; a Nyansa IV where she applies "The Long Correction" herself (the way Kazi VI hands Tunji's method to Zola/Bakari) would be the first transmission entry for an Mji ability.
  4. **Kiti:** the chief aide (she, Kiti II/III) is present at every turning point of Owusu's arc and is the obvious vehicle for a post-resignation Kiti IV testing whether anything of the institution survives him — PH2-059's cost says no; the project has already done this exact beat for Uhuru (`MCD-517`, the successor finds "The Override" didn't pass), so a Kiti version should deliberately differ (e.g., the aide, not a successor).
  5. **Kazi:** Kazi VI explicitly leaves Tunji "not yet approached" the tray-carrying stranger — a deliberate open thread where Tunji eventually tries to vet *Kanja*, which would be a genuinely new register for the unnamed-guest convention (someone trying to read him by the same slow method and finding nothing to read). Flag for Abad before anyone drafts it, since it brushes the convention.
  6. The five territory profile docs (`territory-kazi.md` etc.) are all still missing; Kazi at 13 entries and the only Mji territory with a supporting cast is the natural first backfill under the Launch Protocol, and this report's Kazi timeline (above) can seed its Rules Walkthrough.

  - Rules read in full: 42 (PH2-050–066 = 17; MCD = 25). Plus PH2-034/048/049, MCD-313, MCD-1855, CC-147, MCD-364 for cross-checks.

  - Files touched by the recommended mechanical fixes: Kazi II, VIII, IX, X, XI(none), XIII; Taifa II; Kiti II, III; ledger rules MCD-472, MCD-1528–1532, PH2-051 (and optionally the 71 category tags). Eleven Drive docs would need re-sync afterward (Kazi II, VIII, IX, X, XII? no — IX–XIII headers all change, so IX, X, XI, XII, XIII; plus Kazi II, VIII; Taifa II; Kiti II, III = 10 docs).
  - Methodology notes for the roadmap's consolidation pass: (a) the Batch 139–150 Chronicle II files for *all 12 territories* use unprefixed filenames and H1 titles (e.g. `# The Oath He Didn't Mean` with no "Taifa Chronicle II:" prefix) — any future chunk selection by `<territory>-chronicle-*` glob silently drops them, exactly the lossy-selection problem the Bane pilot warned about; build chunk lists from ledger file references, not globs. You are applying fixes to a locked canon corpus for a long-running fiction-canon project ("My Rival's Distance: The Lords of Cian"), repo root /home/user/Lords-of-Cian-Knowledge-Core. A Fable-model agent already did a read-only review of the Detroit homage-era Territory Chronicles (Kazi, Taifa, Hekalu, Nyansa, Kiti) and produced exact findings and fix instructions below. Your job is to APPLY those fixes exactly as instructed.

IMPORTANT ground rules:
- Edit the Chronicle .md files under docs/lords-of-cian/chronicles/. Note: four second-entry files have NO territory prefix: the-oath-he-didnt-mean.md (Taifa II), the-meal-that-bound-nothing.md (Hekalu II), the-cost-of-being-corrected.md (Nyansa II), the-weeks-the-chair-sat-empty.md (Kiti II).
- Do NOT touch canon-ledger.json directly and do NOT run git commands. Do NOT run it — write, py_compile check, leave for orchestrator. Read the actual current rule statement text from canon-ledger.json first before writing each amendment (several below are substring replacements within a larger statement — read the full current text, then write the full corrected text as the new AMENDMENTS value).
- For every Chronicle file you edit, add a short italic correction note to its header (house style, e.g. "Corrected Batch 342, 2026-10-02: ...").
- Report a concise summary when done: files changed, rule IDs amended, what was deliberately skipped.

**C1 (world-bleed — the Sealbound Directorate doesn't belong in the homage World).**
File the-oath-he-didnt-mean.md (Taifa II): find "a Directorate patrol cornered him" -> "an outside patrol, sent by the claimed land's hostile neighbors, cornered him".
Rule statement amendment (merge script): MCD-472 — find and replace "tempted into betrayal by a Directorate patrol" with "tempted into betrayal by a hostile outside patrol" (read exact current text first).

**C2 (floor-size number conflation — 4,000 readers vs. 200 workers on the halt itself).**
File kazi-chronicle-ii-the-names-beside-his.md: find "You gave four thousand men a way to feel the floor beneath them shift" -> "You gave two hundred men a way to feel the floor beneath them shift"; find "the same week four thousand men found out they could move as one" -> "the same week the whole floor found out it could move as one". File kazi-chronicle-x-the-man-who-mapped-the-door.md (or whichever Kazi X file matches — check the actual title, it may be different from Umoja's identically-named file; search Kazi-prefixed files for "a halt that four thousand men feel at once"): find "a halt that four thousand men feel at once" -> "a halt that two hundred men feel at once".

**C3 (timeline placement fix — header only).**
In the Kazi IX file (search Kazi-prefixed files for a header containing "set in the months before Irin ever called a halt from his own station"): replace that header clause "set in the months before Irin ever called a halt\nfrom his own station." (line wrapping may vary) with "set after the events of Kazi Chronicle I (`MCD-351`)." No prose change needed.

**C4 (intra-arc contradiction — Femi's seat: unpaid vs. salaried).**
In the Kazi XIII file: find "Office, salary line, five-man vote." -> "Office hours, a five-man vote, a desk the rest of us never sit at."; find "The salary line's smaller than the shop floor rate you left. I could put both numbers side by side, plain," -> "The hours that seat eats would earn you more on the floor than it's ever paid you back. I could put both numbers side by side, plain,".

**C5 (stale timeline figure).**
File the-weeks-the-chair-sat-empty.md (Kiti II): find "six years of accumulated institutional weight" -> "two decades of accumulated institutional weight".

**E1 (ordinal-count fix across five Femi-arc entries — this is the biggest single fix set).**
Find the Kazi Chronicles IX through XIII files (search by content: IX currently self-describes as "Fourth Kazi territory Chronicle"/"the fourth entry"; X as "Fifth"/"fifth entry"; XI as "Sixth"/"sixth entry"; XII as "Seventh"/"seventh entry"; XIII as "Eighth"/"eighth entry" — these are WRONG, they should be ninth through thirteenth since Chronicles IV-VIII already correctly claim fourth-eighth). - X file: "fifth" -> "tenth" / "Fifth" -> "Tenth"
- XI file: "sixth" -> "eleventh" / "Sixth" -> "Eleventh"
- XII file: "seventh" -> "twelfth" / "Seventh" -> "Twelfth"
- XIII file: "eighth" -> "thirteenth" / "Eighth" -> "Thirteenth"
Be careful to only change ordinal-count self-references to the Chronicle's own position in the series, not any other unrelated use of those words (unlikely but check context).

Rule statement amendments (merge script), matching the above:
- MCD-1528: find "the fourth entry" -> "the ninth entry"; find "Fourth Kazi territory Chronicle" -> "Ninth Kazi territory Chronicle" (read exact current text first, apply both substitutions to the full statement).

- MCD-1530: "sixth" -> "eleventh" (both occurrences in the statement).
- MCD-1531: "seventh" -> "twelfth" (both occurrences).
- MCD-1532: "eighth" -> "thirteenth" (both occurrences).

**E2 (misattributed incident — wrong rank and wrong timing).**
In the Kazi VIII file: find "the plant manager who'd docked three men's pay over his own scheduling error, the same manager from the gantry season, still unpunished" -> "the line supervisor who'd docked three men's pay over his own scheduling error, back before the gantry walkout, still unpunished".

**E3 (ability cross-bleed — wrong character's signature trait attributed).**
In the Kiti III file: find "every obstruction he'd worn down over the years" -> "every attrition campaign he'd outlasted over the years".

**E5 (stale rule clause, superseded by later-locked characters).**
Rule statement amendment (merge script): PH2-051 — find the clause "Two lieutenants ... stand as his founding co-organizers, not yet individually named or detailed" (read exact current full text first) and replace with wording to the effect of: "stand as his founding co-organizers -- Kunle (PH2-063) and Kalamu (PH2-064); his in-plant organizing partner Tunji (PH2-065) and trustee-seat holder Femi (PH2-066) were added in Batch 287." (integrate naturally into the full statement, don't just insert a fragment — read the whole current PH2-051 text and write the corrected full version).

## NEEDS ABAD — DO NOT APPLY, LEAVE COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED
- D1: the "Torvald" naming-convention question (a possible Old Norse name outside the project's Black/brown-diasporic naming palette) — do not rename, leave as-is in Kazi V and Kazi VIII and their rule statements.
- D2: whether to fold Hekalu III/Taifa II-III/Kiti III's extensions back into PH2-055/053/059's own base rule text — skip, no ledger changes for this.
- D3: tech-register idiom polish ("clocked in," "paychecks," etc.) — low priority, skip entirely.
- E4 (category-tag normalization) — skip, this is being handled corpus-wide separately by the orchestrating session, not per-city.
- E6 (minor prose nit, Kazi X "eleven days' worth of pages") — skip, cosmetic, not required.
- All ENRICHMENT items — skip entirely, not your task.

After applying everything, report back a concise summary.

You are doing a read-only contradiction/error/enrichment review for a long-running canon-locking project ("My Rival's Distance: The Lords of Cian" by Abad Morel), repo root /home/user/Lords-of-Cian-Knowledge-Core. Pay special attention to the "Phase 1" through "Phase 4" sections near the end, which describe the review methodology and error classes already found and fixed across the project's Chronicle tracks (Trinity-era gear anachronisms, pronoun drift, proper-noun collisions, writers'-room leaks, stale age-arithmetic, naming collisions, category-field drift, world-bleed between the mainline World and the homage-era World, etc. — these recur constantly).

## Your scope: Phase 5 of a corpus-wide review roadmap — the CULT, ASH, and SBD rule-prefix blocks

Unlike prior phases, this is NOT a Chronicle-file review — it's a review of the underlying institutional/world-mechanics RULES themselves (not narrative prose), checking the `canon-ledger.json` rules for internal consistency, cross-rule contradictions, stale references, and gaps. This covers three related institutional-lore prefixes:
- `CULT-` (~200 rules): the cult ecosystem — Anu Un Ra/T.D.K., the Ever-Haunt classification system, the Domus Inviolate Dossier material, the Anu Un Ra Dossier, Vargo Vakas, the Warbody, the Exchange Protocol, Ghost-Lattice, etc.
- `ASH-` (~57 rules): the Ashkeel institution — the Seven High Arts, the collar/legal hierarchy, the Basalt Codex, internal geography, merchant guilds, named characters.
- `SBD-` (~65 rules): the Sealbound Directorate — Shelton Dexton, Ilona Corrance, the Scrip-Ledger disciplinary system, SEALBLACK detachments, anomaly-class entities, facilities, the Oracle Conflict Map.

## What to do

1. Grep canon-ledger.json for every rule with these three prefixes and read all statements in full.
2. Check for internal contradictions: do any two rules in these blocks assert mutually exclusive facts (numbers, dates, character traits, mechanisms)?
3. Check for stale cross-references: does any rule cite another rule ID that was later superseded, amended, or renumbered, where the citing rule's own text no longer accurately describes the target?
4. Check for terminology/mechanism drift: does a later rule in the same prefix block use an ability/mechanism/institution name inconsistently with how an earlier rule in the same block defined it?
5. Check category-field consistency (each rule dict has an "id", "category", "statement", "status", "source" — grep the actual JSON for the category values used across these three prefixes and flag drift, same pattern as the category-drift fixes already made in Phase 4).
6. Check for proper-noun collisions — do any named characters/places/institutions across these three blocks collide with each other, or with anything outside these blocks (spot-check a sample against the broader ledger)?
7. Check these blocks against any Chronicle prose that dramatizes them (CULT-197/198's countermeasure is dramatized in the Kanja-version track, Phase 3 already reviewed — don't re-review that, just confirm no NEW contradiction surfaces from the ledger side). SBD material is referenced in several Alias Chronicles (Bane, etc.) already reviewed in Phase 1 — don't re-review those files, just check the ledger-side rules for self-consistency.
8. Enrichment: genuine gaps or loose threads worth flagging (not full creative drafting — just noting).

## Output format

CONTRADICTIONS / ERRORS / ENRICHMENT / METRICS. For each finding: exact rule ID(s), precise problem description, recommended fix instruction (exact old text -> new text where possible, since a separate Sonnet-model agent will apply your exact instructions verbatim to canon-ledger.json). Flag anything requiring NEW creative/worldbuilding invention separately — needs Abad's direct approval, not unilateral fixing. Mechanical/reconciliation fixes (stale citations, terminology drift, category normalization, renames to resolve collisions) can be fixed directly per established project precedent.

Do not edit any files. Be thorough but efficient — this is ~320 rules of dense institutional lore, not narrative prose, so reading is faster than a Chronicle review but cross-referencing matters more. Report back in full detail.

## Phase 5: the institutional rule-block fable-review, Batches 340-344, 2026-10-02

Four parallel Fable-model review agents, grouped by rule-prefix family, reviewed the project's
non-Chronicle institutional/world-mechanics rule blocks directly (not narrative prose) -- checking
canon-ledger.json's own rule statements for internal contradictions, stale cross-references,
terminology drift, naming collisions, and category/status-field metadata drift. Findings were then
applied by matching Sonnet fix agents, mirroring the Phase 1-4 pattern. The one deliberately
deferred block: MCD core (~1,800 rules, the project's largest single prefix), given its enormous
scale -- flagged as a future undertaking, not attempted in this pass.

**Batch 340, CC-/WGD-/CHAR- (22 rule statements amended).** Fixes Abyss's "crew's youngest member"
claim against Pyro's own locked age (`CC-101`, `MCD-1715`); reconciles a half-applied Batch-321 fix
where Danne Sok's memory still described Kanja as "freed" rather than found alongside (`CC-159`,
`MCD-530`, `MCD-234`); closes a stale age-ranking gap left by `MCD-1851` (`CC-058`); corrects
`SBD-041`/`MCD-022`'s false-claims lists, which had wrongly flagged Pyro's natural birth as part of
Dexton's lie when `MCD-022` locks it as true; fixes a `CC-088` misattribution (`SBD-048`); removes a
writers'-room leak (`WGD-009`); adds a reconciling clause connecting "the Sovereignty Summit" and
"the Fulfillment Ceremony" as the same event (`MCD-091`, `CC-009`); fixes a citation error, a
garbled sentence, and a wrong rule citation (`CC-148`/`022`/`154`); renames Varruk's "Cadence Ruin"
(later reconciled, see Batch 343). Normalizes category drift across 100 `CC-` rules.

**Batch 341, PH2-/WC-/POL-/VB-/COS- (17 rule statements amended).** Removes two firearms
anachronisms from homage-era definitional rules (`PH2-014`/`016`); updates `PH2-048`'s own
description of the Chronicle-track structure to match the Batch 64 correction, and extends its
survival-applied list to include Sauti and Duro; realizes `PH2-049`'s "not yet drafted" firearms
placeholder against the now-locked `ARS-426`; fixes a stale `WC-018` citation and a `WC-024`/`WC-003`
density-tier table gap; fixes a broken city-rename phrase (`PH2-009`) and two real-world-date leaks
into in-world character facts (`PH2-023`/`042`); extends `VB-026`/`020` to record the Kanja-version
track's narrator assignment and the Alias Chronicle track's deliberate exemption from it; fixes a
Sin-Eater density range mismatch (`CC-105`) and an army-commitment overstatement (`POL-102`).
Normalizes category drift across 42 rules and status drift across 30 rules.

**Batch 342, CULT-/ASH-/SBD- (37 rule statements amended).** Separates Dexton's one accurate claim
(Pyro's natural birth) from his false ones (`SBD-041`); renames an Ashkeel archive register away
from a collision with Onyx's "Black Ledger" power (`ASH-047`); fixes a direct contradiction about
the Null Caucus's relative age (`CULT-156`); corrects a stale post-Batch-103 Maw-7/Karkosa venue
citation (`CULT-140`); fixes a misreading of the Calibration Array's completeness (`CULT-187`); fixes
a depth-direction error in Ashkeel's vertical geography (`ASH-046`); fixes a `GEO-002` region-count
conflation (`ASH-001`); reconciles two names for the Ashkeel founding war (`ASH-010`/`054`/`056`);
rewrites `SBD-010` to distinguish it clearly from `SBD-041` as two separate false SBD narratives;
clarifies in-world SBD asset-designation numbers from this ledger's own `SBD-` rule-ID series
(`SBD-042`/`043`); updates several stale cross-references; removes real-world proper-noun leaks from
seven Ashkeel in-world names; renames three named Ashkeel figures to resolve collisions with
already-locked characters. Normalizes category drift across 47 `CULT-`/`ASH-` rules.

**Batch 343, reconciliation (no new facts).** The Batch 342 Varruk rename ran against a slightly
earlier ledger snapshot than Batch 340's own independent rename of the same ability (Batch 340 chose
"the Riptide Break," Batch 342 chose "Cadence Break" without seeing Batch 340's choice), leaving
`CC-099` referencing a name that no longer existed in `CC-098`. Standardized on "Cadence
Break"/"Cadence Saturation" and corrected `CC-099`'s own cross-reference to match -- a real artifact
of running two parallel rename agents against the same contested name without them seeing each
other's work; worth remembering for any future parallel-rename pass (serialize renames touching the
same proper noun, or have a consolidation step reconcile them, as done here).

**Batch 344, ARS-/MAW-/HLD- (28 rule statements amended).** Corrects four stale "CONFLICT-CHECK"
notes that wrongly placed Ozmund's Maw entry in Book 3 when it's actually locked as Book 1
(`MAW-030`/`100`/`101`, `ARS-270`); fixes a self-contradicting Reclamation venue/date (`MAW-065`,
`MAW-121`); corrects the Unarmed Siege of Maw-3's mechanism to match its own higher-authority source;
reconciles the Grand Circuit's founding date and fixes era-boundary arithmetic (`MAW-091`); fixes
bout-count, Reclamation-date, and patron-house citation errors (`MAW-119`/`120`); corrects a
Cestari-era anachronism and a biology-type mismatch (`MAW-125`/`144`); fixes a tense error treating
an unhappened Book 1 event as already accomplished (`MAW-096`); de-numericizes an internally
inconsistent manumission-rate claim (`MAW-079`); corrects the Trinity's seal-duration arithmetic and
the Moonvault gift split (`ARS-010`/`060`); fixes gear-era label mismatches and several stale/wrong
rule-ID citations. Normalizes category drift on 2 `ARS-` rules and status-field casing on 72 rules
across the three blocks.

Ledger reached `ledger_version` 34.7, 2,650 rules, 344 batches -- zero duplicate IDs verified after
every batch. This closes Phase 5's fable-review-then-fix pass across all five institutional
rule-block groups (CULT/ASH/SBD, CC/WGD/CHAR, ARS/MAW/HLD, PH2/WC/POL/VB/COS). The MCD core block
(~1,800 rules) remains genuinely open for a future dedicated pass -- it was deliberately not
attempted here given its scale relative to everything else reviewed.

**Running tally of items requiring Abad's own direct review, accumulated across Phases 1.5 through
5.** None of these block further work; they're queued for whenever Abad wants a dedicated session:
- **Atlas/geography:** the Verehimu/Voskharen Wetlands naming question; whether "the Karkosa" the
  crew keeps an archive aboard is the Karkosa Complex itself or a distinct base; the Teeth's Atlas
  placement; `MCD-094`'s area-vs-population-weight framing; `MCD-112`'s Southern Seaboard
  definition; a full Portside/Kessic-region/naval-geography/Kesmara/House-Verehimu-seat enrichment
  pass; the Shattered Kingdoms' land-area-vs-political-weight percentage question (`POL-010` vs
  `WC-012` vs `MCD-094`).
- **Character Chronicle tracks:** Ezio's true age (`CC-028`'s "75" vs. two tracks implying ~309);
  whether Fermand is a sixth knower of Ezio's classified capability; the Lauris dockside-crew-
  mortality question (several Strand W entries show crew alive centuries past their locked
  mortality elsewhere -- the single largest open item from the whole Phase 2 pass); whether "Vask
  Ilvane" is a 13th Vask or an outlying Hold; Vael Korr-Drennen's gender (a 3-2 split in the
  corpus); the Ozmund/Book-1 placement question in two Lauris Strand W entries; VB-020/VB-023 vs
  CC-034's standing Ezio-narrator conflict.
- **Kanja-version track:** a standing age-band convention for Onyx's `VB-026` presence growth;
  whether narrator codas should be first-person or "the blade" third-person by age; locking
  Ironbane's (and possibly Soulreaver Zora's) Rebellion-era joining date; naming the custodial
  apparatus Auberon is handed to.
- **Territory Chronicles:** Xaragua Chronicle III's cohort death count; Orin's phonograph/
  pressed-record anachronism; the "Torvald" naming-convention question; several near-collision names
  (Guaní/Guanín, Kasa/Kasi, Tunji/Tunde) flagged but not renamed.
- **Institutional rules:** the CULT block's "T.D.K. returned and was immediately contained at the
  Great Breach" framing across 16 rules, which conflicts with the locked Book 2-5 arc (the single
  largest structural question surfaced in Phase 5); ASH-018 vs WC-011 on where Trust Scrip
  circulates in the Shattered Kingdoms; Matar's recruitment date and Orlok's timeline (both `CC-`
  internal contradictions needing a numeric pick); Valen's age contradiction (a locked `MCD-248`
  origin scene); the Ghost-Lattice/Silent Mara chronology hedge; three further numeric picks (House
  Brekka's founding date, Lady Aravel's age, Essek Nightfall's date); Osseren's Pillar-reinstatement
  question; "the Patient Stone" cross-block naming collision; COS-001's "Vakas power" vs "the Vault"
  ambiguity; roughly a dozen further near-collision character names.

input.prompt:
You are doing a read-only contradiction/error/enrichment review for a long-running canon-locking project ("My Rival's Distance: The Lords of Cian" by Abad Morel), repo root /home/user/Lords-of-Cian-Knowledge-Core. Read /home/user/Lords-of-Cian-Knowledge-Core/CLAUDE.md in full first for project context, conventions, and history — it's very long, that's expected, it's the authoritative batch-by-batch log. Pay special attention to the "Phase 1" through "Phase 5" sections near the end, which describe the review methodology and error classes already found and fixed across the project (Trinity-era gear anachronisms, pronoun drift, proper-noun collisions, writers'-room leaks, stale age-arithmetic, naming collisions, category-field drift, world-bleed between worlds, real-world proper-noun leaks, stale cross-references, etc.).

## Your scope: Phase 5 continuation — MCD core rules MCD-001 through MCD-450

This is the final, largest remaining chunk of a corpus-wide review roadmap. MCD- is the project's largest rule prefix (~1,800 rules total, split into four chunks for review — you have the first quarter by ID number). These are foundational "world mechanics" facts: core canon decisions, character backstories, battle accounts, geography, the Twenty-Two Victories, the Long Mask Chronicles, the World Adaptation Blueprint material, etc. Unlike Chronicle files, these are NOT narrative prose — they're dense factual rule statements, already cross-checked extensively by every Chronicle-track review in Phases 1-4 (so Chronicle-level contradictions in this range are unlikely to have survived — focus on contradictions WITHIN and BETWEEN these MCD rules themselves, and against other prefix blocks already reviewed in Phase 5).

Read: grep canon-ledger.json for every rule with id MCD-001 through MCD-450 and read all statements in full. This is a lot of rules — you don't need to memorize every detail, but do read every statement text.

## What to check

1. **Internal contradictions**: do any two rules in this range assert mutually exclusive facts (dates, ages, casualty counts, character traits, geography, mechanisms)? The project has a known history of early-batch material (pre-batch-log era) sometimes containing stale figures that later-batch material superseded without the earlier rule being updated — check for this pattern specifically.
2. **Stale cross-references**: does any rule cite another rule ID whose content has since changed, been renamed, or been superseded, making the citation inaccurate?
3. **Terminology/naming drift**: does a name, place, or mechanism get used inconsistently across different rules in this range?
4. **Category/status field drift**: grep the actual JSON for "category" and "status" values across MCD-001 through MCD-450 and flag inconsistent/stale values (null categories, uppercase "LOCKED" status, etc.) — same pattern already fixed in Phases 1-5 for other prefixes.
5. **Proper-noun collisions**: spot-check named characters/places introduced in this range against the rest of the ledger (you don't need to check every single name — focus on anything that looks newly-coined or unusual).
6. **Cross-reference against already-reviewed Phase 5 blocks** (CULT-/ASH-/SBD-/CC-/ARS-/MAW-/HLD-/PH2-/WC-/POL-/VB-/COS-, all already fixed) — does anything in MCD-001-450 conflict with a fact Phase 5 already locked/corrected in those blocks? (You don't need to re-read those blocks in full — if you recall something from CLAUDE.md's Phase 5 summary that seems relevant, cross-check it.)
7. Real-world proper-noun leaks, writers'-room leaks inside rule statements.
8. Enrichment: genuine gaps worth flagging (not drafting).

## Output format

CONTRADICTIONS / ERRORS / ENRICHMENT / METRICS. For each finding: exact rule ID(s), precise problem description, recommended fix instruction (exact old text -> new text where possible, since a Sonnet-model agent will apply your instructions verbatim). Flag anything requiring NEW creative/worldbuilding invention separately — needs Abad's direct approval. Mechanical/reconciliation fixes (stale citations, category normalization, obvious arithmetic errors) can be fixed directly per established project precedent.

Do not edit any files. This is a large chunk (~450 rules) — be efficient: skim for patterns rather than deeply analyzing every single rule, but don't skip entire sections. Report back in full detail, but keep your report focused on genuine findings rather than exhaustively cataloging everything you read.

1	# Lords of Cian Interactive Archive — Game Plan, Backlog & Engagement Roadmap
2	
3	By Abad Morel. Fleet-reviewed strategy deliverable, adversarial + Opus 5 synthesis, reconciled from three source documents (Visual Direction Document v1.0, System Explanation, Strategy Document), drafted in parallel, adversarially reviewed, and synthesized into one execution-ready plan.
4	
5	Date: 20 August 2026. Status: Reconciled final. Source repository: The-Reaver/My-Rivals-Distance-Archive.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## §0 Executive Summary
10	
11	Ground truth: the three source documents describe a nearly-finished system; the connected GitHub repository (The-Reaver/My-Rivals-Distance-Archive) is empty, zero commits, zero branches on origin, no src/, no package.json, no migrations. Everything described in the System Explanation exists only inside the Lovable workspace, so no claim in its "Complete" list can be independently verified, and no engineer other than Lovable's own agent can review, test, or safely modify the codebase.
12	
13	Two live risks sit behind that wall: the source document contradicts itself on whether Row Level Security is actually enabled (§3 and §9's Complete list say yes; §9's Remaining Step 8 says re-enable it), and email confirmation is disabled by design (§7), meaning the demand signal the entire strategy is built to trust (request counts, referral chains, registered-user totals) can currently be manufactured by one person with a script. Everything below is sequenced behind these three facts. The work itself is not large; the ordering is what matters.
14	
15	Standing caveat: table names, the 11 document types, and clearance rules below are quoted from the source documents. Individual column names and file paths are unverified until the repo sync (P0-1) lands; treat any field-level reference as "assumed, confirm on sync."
16	
17	---
18	
19	## §1 Game Plan
20	
21	Six phases. Each names the backlog items it executes, full detail in the Stock Recommendation below.
22	
23	### Phase 0 — Establish ground truth
24	Executes P0-1, P0-2.
25	
26	Push the Lovable project into GitHub, then run a single read-only audit pass over the real code against the eight documented contradictions and one orphan table listed under P0-2. Nothing gets built in this phase, the output is a decision record, written into CLAUDE.md alongside the Visual Direction tokens, so every later phase is verifying rather than guessing.
27	
28	Also here, because it's nearly free: confirm the Supabase service-role key and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY don't appear in any file about to enter version control, and rotate the Anthropic key as hygiene now that the codebase is entering a second platform.
29	
30	Done when: git log on origin shows real history; the src/ tree matches System Explanation §8 or the differences are documented; CLAUDE.md carries the Visual Direction tokens and the resolved decisions; no secrets in the diff.
31	
32	### Phase 1 — Lock the database and the signal
33	Executes P0-3, P0-4. Designs P1-1.
34	
35	Security is sequenced first, not after feature completion. The archive is already deployed to a lovable.app URL anyone holding the link can reach, and the anon key ships in the browser bundle where its only protection is RLS. If RLS is off or permissive, which §9 Step 8 implies, reader emails, engagement rows, and the referral graph are exposed today, not at launch.
36	
37	Baseline default-deny RLS across all 11 tables now, with per-table clearance-aware read policies, extending the policy set as each new route lands in Phase 2. Alongside it, close the identity hole (P0-4): a demand signal that can be faked is worse than no signal, and the platform's stated identity is "honest by design" (Strategy §9).
38	
39	One coupling to resolve before writing policies: per-row lockdown on requests and engagement collides with the public UI displaying aggregates of that same data (follower count and Reader Demand Score on the character hero, Visual Direction §4; Character Index sorted by demand score, §6). Design the public aggregate (P1-1) here, so policies are written around it, not against it.
40	
41	Done when: a Supabase security-advisor pass returns no RLS warnings on any of the 11 tables; a Level 1 test account cannot read Level 2/3 content, another user's profile row, or the referral graph; book-placement spoiler enforcement survives a direct SQL/API attempt bypassing the admin UI; a scripted signup cannot inflate a request count, a referral chain, or the registered-user total.
42	
43	### Phase 2 — Complete the reader loop
44	Executes P1-1 through P1-6.
45	
46	The gaps the source document names itself (Steps 5, 6, 7), plus two the documents imply but never scope: a public demand aggregate (P1-1) and an extraction tool (P1-3), the more important find. The entire content architecture rests on "reader-facing content is a curated slice... extracted from the source material" (Strategy §3): a physical description pulled from a Character Codex, a weapon promoted to a world briefing (System Explanation §4). But no admin section performs extraction, and no remaining build step creates one. Intake routes everything except Chronicle Entries into archive_documents and stops, without extraction, writer-reference content has no path to readers except retyping, and Phase 5's unlock cascade has no legal mechanism at all.
47	
48	Done when: a Level 1+ reader can browse /archive and read /archive/:id gated by the clearance set at intake; an admin can extract a section from a writer-reference document into a new reader-facing row without altering the source row's storage mode; an admin can paste full chronicle prose into a side-by-side editor and publish it; a public visitor sees a demand score on a character profile while per-row reader data stays unreadable.
49	
50	### Phase 3 — Launch
51	Executes P1-7.
52	
53	Content-readiness gate first: enough Level 0/1 material live to make "pre-book content is a full world, not a teaser" (Strategy §4) true, briefings across the confirmed category set, arsenal entries, and enough chronicle entries beyond the 10 seed rows that a Level 1 reader can plausibly read three to 90%, since that action is load-bearing for Level 2. Then deploy, connect the domain, and run a full four-level QA pass on a disposable account against the Level 2 rule confirmed in Phase 0, not against both readings, and not against whichever one a draft assumed.
54	
55	Done when: production URL live on the custom domain; all four clearance transitions verified end-to-end; a test request appears correctly in the Demand panel within the session; the landing page matches whichever landing-page resolution Phase 0 recorded.

57	### Phase 4 — Operate the demand engine

59	
60	The steady state, not a task. Neither source document specifies a review cadence, only that the Demand panel carries 7-day and 30-day trend windows; weekly is a recommendation because it matches the shorter window, not a source mandate.
61	
62	Each cycle: read the Demand panel by trend direction, not raw total (a 150-rising character outranks a 200-flat one, per Strategy §6); check clearance distribution as the diagnostic §6 says it is; check referral chain depth for network structure; and, new from Phase 1, check the anomaly flag before trusting any spike. Feed the resulting priority stack back into the extraction and chronicle-editor tooling from Phase 2.
63	
64	Done when (recurring): every newly-developed pending character traces back to a documented demand decision, count, trend, engagement, and a clean anomaly check.
65	
66	### Phase 5 — The Book 1 unlock cascade
67	Consumes P1-3 and P0-3. No new backlog items.
68	
69	When Book 1 ships, mark it published in admin_settings. Per Strategy §7 the cascade makes Book-1-tagged vault items eligible to go live, subject to author review.
70	
71	Correction carried from review: an earlier draft proposed publishing Book-1-tagged Threat Blueprint and Tactical Architecture content directly. Both are Writer-Reference, "system-stored, admin-searchable, never publishable" (Strategy §3). Nothing flips a Writer-Reference row to Live. The correct action is extraction: pull the relevant Book-1 material into new Chronicle Entries or archive documents via the P1-3 tool, leaving the source rows untouched. This is exactly why P1-3 is not optional.

73	Re-run the Phase 3 QA against this transition specifically, the first time the platform operates in companion mode rather than predecessor mode, and the first live test of book-placement enforcement under real pressure.
74	
75	Done when: published_books reflects Book 1; Book-1-derived content is live; Book 2-5 content remains vault-locked and unreachable by direct URL or API; Level 3 structural-reveal content has been re-read to confirm it still lands now that Book 1 exists.
76	
77	The post-series fan-contribution framework (Strategy §7) sits past this horizon, scope it when Book 5 is in sight, not now.
78

136	## §3 Interactive & Engagement Improvements
137	
138	Ranked by expected impact on the demand signal. Every item extends a mechanic that already exists, clearance, requests, the single-character follow, the referral chain, rather than bolting on points, streaks, or badges. None introduces a carousel, an icon in primary navigation, a box shadow, a gradient on an interactive surface, or a tooltip; JetBrains Mono stays confined to metric values.
139	
140	Two preconditions apply to the whole section: all schema references are unverified until P0-1, and items 1 and 5 make gameable metrics more public and more decision-critical, neither ships before P0-4.
141	
142	1. **The Standing Requests Ledger.** Blocked on P0-4. Make the request count reader-visible on a pending character's profile as an in-world ledger, "47 readers have requested this Chronicle," with an optional one-line reason the requester typed, rendered as a plain vertical feed. Signal: converts a private admin metric into a public commitment device, compounding the exact number Strategy §6 uses to pick what gets written next. Build note: needs a pending-character stat bar variant (Requests + reason feed only); the four-metric bar in Visual Direction §4 assumes engagement history a pending character has none of.
143	
144	2. **Request Fulfillment Loop.** When a requested character's first chronicle entry goes live, every reader holding a request for that character gets one quiet Activity Feed item, timestamped, styled like any other release notice, plus an email. No confetti, no unlock animation. Correction: trigger is the chronicle entry's own live flag flipping true, not the book-publication toggle. Everything in the archive is pre-book by design (Strategy §4); the published_books toggle governs the Book 2-5 vault cascade and would never fire for this feature's primary case. Signal: closes the self-feeding cycle Strategy §6 describes but nothing currently enforces.
145	
146	3. **Field Notes.** Inside the Chronicle Reader, a reader marks a paragraph as significant, framed as adding it to their own dossier, not as a like. Plain text affordance on hover at the standard 150ms, no icon. Marked passages collect in the reader's private profile. Signal: progress tracking currently records scroll percentage and a completion flag (entry-level). Passage marking gives paragraph-level resolution on which beats land. Build note: markdown bodies have no stable paragraph identity; anchoring needs a deterministic scheme (content hash or index plus fallback) or every body edit orphans every note against it.
147	
148	4. **Also Drawn To.** Signup forces one followed character, a strong signal per Strategy §5, but one that discards everyone's second interest across an 18-character roster. Add an optional, non-required list a reader can build from the Character Index at any time. Plain text-link additions, vertical feed. Signal: reveals cross-character affinity clusters, readers who follow A but circle back to C are a distinct segment from A-exclusive readers, telling you which pending character's audience overlaps an already-engaged base.
149	
150	5. **The Referral Lineage.** Blocked on P0-4. At Level 3, render the reader's actual chain as a short in-world genealogy: "Brought in by ___. You brought in: ___." Text only, Inter, no tree diagram, no badge. Signal: Strategy §6 calls referral "the only compounding marketing channel" and wants chain depth; nothing currently surfaces it. Showing it rewards the behavior and, through the same query used in P2-3, tells you which Level 3 readers actually compound versus refer once and stop. Build note: chain depth is a recursive query, not an index.
151	
152	6. **Correspondence Checkpoints.** Wire the 11 seeded quiz questions into a short in-world "correspondence" a reader completes after finishing a character's arc. Results feed the diagnostic dashboard; they do not gate clearance. Corrections upheld: Level 2 unlocks connective tissue, Level 3 unlocks structural reveals; both stay deliberately distinct, so a quiz gating "Level 2/3" conflates two tiers. Gating access behind a graded test is a genuinely new mechanic, the only item here that fails this section's own selection criterion, and it puts the reader in the position of being evaluated, against Strategy §8's non-gamified posture. Uncapped retries make a pass-rate meaningless. Resolution: keep the feature, drop the gate. Count first attempts only toward the pass-rate diagnostic; allow unlimited retries for the reader's own satisfaction, flagged separately. Signal: per-question first-try pass rate tells you which world element is confusing readers, the fine-grained tool the clearance diagnostic currently lacks.
153	
154	7. **Follow Reconsideration.** Allow one follow change after a fixed window, say 30 days, presented plainly as "Follow a different character instead." Not an achievement, not a reset. Explicit rule: switching resets Level 3 progress toward the new character; completion history against the previous character is preserved for analytics only and does not count toward clearance. Without this, Level 3 has undefined, and exploitable, behavior mid-arc. Signal: a switch from A to B is itself the data point, sharper than either character's raw follow count; the current schema throws it away by overwriting the field silently.
155	
156	8. **Connective Tissue Trails.** Passively log which cross-links (character-to-faction, faction-to-institution, character-to-character) readers actually click through in the Level 2 world briefings. Invisible to the reader. Correction: this is a schema change. Engagement events are documented as "type label + entity ID" with no metadata column anywhere in the source material; scope it as adding a metadata JSON column, confirmed against the real schema on sync. Signal: maps which relationships readers are curious about, not just which characters, per §6's "deepest following" criterion.
157	
158	9. **Two Dossiers, Side by Side.** Let a reader select exactly two characters on the Index and view their dossier-cover data statically side by side. Comparison is a purchase-consideration signal, "I'm choosing between these two," distinct from a request. Corrections: the symmetric two-character layout is new, not inherited (Visual Direction §4's Lore Panel is an asymmetric 60/40 split for a single character, say "visually consistent with the card system," not "reuses the Lore Panel"). Shares item 8's metadata-column dependency: a pair of character IDs doesn't fit a single entity-ID field.

281	  lone authority handing down doctrine — the "anything large enough to be seen is large enough to
282	  be burned" principle is reached through open argument within the five-person founding core
283	  (Ch. VII), and later genuinely challenged again by Kether without being cleanly refuted
284	  (Ch. XXXIX). He is shown conceding partial ground under a good-faith internal case more than once,
285	  not simply proven right.
286	- **Teaching that survives the teacher.** A recurring, explicit throughline: teaching is framed as
287	  successful specifically when "it keeps working after the teacher stops watching" (Ch. XXIV) — the
288	  forging-lineage arc (Block G) ends with a forger three teaching-generations removed from Daba who
289	  has never heard his name (Ch. XXXV), and the network arc (Block F) ends with Daba's own role
290	  shifted from operator to architect who "deliberately no longer knows every face in the network"
291	  (Ch. XXX).
292	- **Costs shown as real losses, not disguised wins.** Block H is explicit and unsoftened about
293	  this: Tamsin dies in custody because Daba refuses a rescue that would expose three cells
294	  (Ch. XXXVI); Pallow's Reach saves roughly half a settlement and loses the other half, a cost "the
295	  entry does not resolve into a hidden win" (Ch. XXXVIII); Ilyse loses a nine-year cover identity,
296	  its business, and its relationships on eleven days' notice (Ch. XXXVII). This is stated policy
297	  for the corpus, not an accident — a psychological profile should take the recurring cost/doubt
298	  register seriously rather than smoothing it into pure competence.
299	- **Relationship pattern: intimacy and trust are always earned slowly, never assumed.** This holds
300	  for 1804's own recruits (the yearlong vetting of Isolde Wrenna, the sealed-second structure that
301	  never tells a person they've been chosen until it matters) and for the mentorship with Kanja
302	  itself, which opens on "deliberate mutual wariness rather than any trust" (Ch. XI) and only
303	  becomes a stated trade between equals once both parties say so aloud (Ch. XIV).
304	- **Voice/register.** Patient, arithmetic-minded, comfortable holding unresolved doubt rather than
305	  forcing resolution (Ch. XL's "neither the doubt nor the determination resolves the other" is the
306	  clearest single statement of this). Not without warmth — Ch. XLVIII ("The Bet Daba Wasn't
307	  Supposed to Win") is explicit that 1804 is "a home with real affection and levity in it, not only
308	  doctrine and grief," and shows Daba genuinely, accidentally laughed into unguarded amusement.
309	- **Named characters, full list:** see the Relationships section above for the complete,
310	  block-by-block roster (Fennic, Mika, Odalys, Sana, Torvin, Sael, Corvin, Nessa, Farro, Ketra,
311	  Riasa Vorn, Rhyne Cadec, Yeva Tolan, Marn, Bramm Oskell, Isolde Wrenna, Coen, Sabeth, Marrek, Wren
312	  Talsen, Ilse Corvane, Tamsin, Halvin, Bren, Farel, Ilyse, Mattis Kastel, Serel, Kether, Deryn
313	  Kettel, Orsk Dresk, Elowen Sarn, Halvar Ilven, Tobin Cray, Quill Vantry, Perrin, Tessin).
314	- **What should constrain the Psychological Profile.** The corpus already establishes a stated core
315	  wound (the Rookery itself, and specifically the private, unresolved "tally" he keeps of every
316	  name lost to the doctrine's own arithmetic, Ch. XL) and a stated defining doctrine (discipline
317	  over mass, distrust of anything large enough to be seen or any single point — person, forge, or
318	  cell — that the whole depends on). A profile pass should treat these as already-demonstrated
319	  facts to build on, not as open questions to invent from scratch. What genuinely remains open and
320	  under-dramatized: his relationship to his own privately-carried doubt (only Ch. XL goes there
321	  directly across 50 entries); whether the Kether challenge changed him in any lasting way; and
322	  what, if anything, he wants for himself beyond the network's survival — no entry in the corpus
323	  addresses a personal want or hope distinct from 1804's own mission.
